a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Computationally Bounded Knowledge ... Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K) ... Explicit != Derivable != Available ... This is not UNKNOWN in the same sense as absence of representation. It is a computational boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-4 (section 5): distinguishes Cn_S(K) (all consequences) from Avail_S(K,B) (what a bounded reasoning process can actually compute), with Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K), giving a three-way distinction Explicit != Derivable != Available; a proposition can be derivable-but-unavailable, which is a computational-boundary phenomenon, explicitly NOT the same kind of UNKNOWN as absence of representation. Flagged as feeding the future Zero/Evaluation model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'failure to derive' as a typed epistemic distinction ... U_rep, U_der, U_avail, U_evid, U_eval, U_scope ... We do not need to make these six values of one enum ... we should not flatten them. Instead EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) remains the better direction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 9 (feeding FR-3/FR-4): distinguishes six typed causes of epistemic failure-to-derive -- U_rep (not represented), U_der (not derivable under S), U_avail (derivable but resource-unavailable), U_evid (insufficient evidence), U_eval (evaluation cannot determine), U_scope (outside declared scope) -- explicitly refusing to flatten them into one enum, per prior FDE/Zero experiments, and reaffirming the structured EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) direction as better than a flat value set. Grounded in the Handbook's observation that incomplete reasoning and incomplete knowledge can have different causes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 1: The Foundational Epistemic Pipeline -- FR-1 Representation Separation [STRONG], FR-2 Reasoning Relativity [STRONG], FR-3 Epistemic Processing Separation [STRONG], FR-4 Bounded Derivation [STRONG]
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 1 formalizes FR-1 through FR-4 with explicit [STRONG] status labels and 'Promote to theory principle/invariant' actions: FR-1 K^exp != K^der; FR-2 Derive_S(K,q) with S=(L,Sigma,R,Sem,B); FR-3 Query != Reasoning != Evaluation != Determination with Sat != ASK, Sat != Truth, Determination != Truth; FR-4 Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K), Explicit != Derivable != Available.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-1.3 Explicit vs. Implicit Knowledge ... Explicit(phi) iff phi in K; Implicit(phi) iff phi not-in K and K entails phi. Tractability: O(1) for explicit; NP-hard in general for implicit deduction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds D-1.3 Explicit-vs-Implicit Knowledge to the R_req inventory (Tier P1): Explicit(phi) iff phi in K; Implicit(phi) iff phi not-in K and K entails phi; explicit lookup is O(1), implicit deduction is NP-hard in general -- connecting this batch's FR-1/K^exp-K^der distinction into the R_req formal distinction inventory with a stated complexity class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What the research has also confirmed: TRUE != BELIEVED != KNOWN, Explicit != Implicit, Stored != Derived != Entailed, Observed != Inferred != Reported, NoEvidence != NotAssessed, Unresolved != False, NoKnownGap != Complete, Representation != Reality. The report explicitly lists these as Tier-1 corpus distinctions ... R_req is becoming a unifying framework for distinctions discovered across the KnowledgeOS research program.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes that the reviewed report consolidates eight distinctions already independently discovered elsewhere in the KnowledgeOS research program (TRUE!=BELIEVED!=KNOWN, Explicit!=Implicit, Stored!=Derived!=Entailed, Observed!=Inferred!=Reported, NoEvidence!=NotAssessed, Unresolved!=False, NoKnownGap!=Complete, Representation!=Reality) as Tier-1 corpus distinctions, positioning R_req as a unifying framework rather than an isolated new idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence -> Representation -> Reasoning -> Evaluation -> Determination ... Representation, Reasoning, Evaluation and Determination are distinct semantic functions. No result produced by one function is automatically equivalent to the result of another. Formally: Rep != Reason != Eval != Det. This should become a theory-level principle, not merely a candidate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central addition #1: make explicit the chain Evidence -> Representation -> Reasoning -> Evaluation -> Determination as a semantic separation of distinct epistemic functions (not merely an architectural pipeline); proposes the theory-level principle Rep != Reason != Eval != Det, citing the Handbook's distinction of knowledge representation from reasoning mechanisms and from task-level knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add Explicit vs Derived Knowledge ... K_t^{exp} and K_t^{der,S} with K_t^{der,S}=Cn_S(K_t^{exp}) ... K^{exp}!=K^{der} and Derivability does not imply operational availability. Therefore K^{der,S} != K^{available,S}.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-1 (section 2): defines K_t^exp (explicit) and K_t^der,S = Cn_S(K_t^exp) (derived under reasoning system S) as distinct conceptual layers; states K^exp != K^der and that derivability does not imply operational availability, so K^der,S != K^available,S. Grounded in the Handbook's distinction between explicit beliefs and logical-closure consequences, and the problem of logical omniscience. Status: STRONG.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add the Reasoning-System parameter S ... K |-_S p ... S=(L,Sigma,R,Sem,B) ... We should not claim this tuple is the final KnowledgeOS definition of a ReasoningSystem ... neg Derive_S(K,p) does not entail neg p. And neg Derive_S(K,p) does not even necessarily entail neg Derivable_S(K,p). That distinction is extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-2 (section 3): derivability should be indexed by a reasoning regime, Derive_S(K,p) rather than absolute K|-p, with S conceptually = (L representation language, Sigma vocabulary/signature, R inference rules, Sem semantics, B computational/resource boundary) explicitly NOT claimed as the final KnowledgeOS ReasoningSystem definition. Important consequence: not-Derive_S(K,p) entails neither not-p nor not-Derivable_S(K,p) -- a distinction flagged as extremely important for Zero and UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Query != Evaluation != Determination ... ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult ... Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal ... Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination ... We must not define Sat = ASK or Sat = Truth or Determination = Truth. This should become an explicit KnowledgeOS invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-3 (section 4): promotes Query != Evaluation != Determination from research observation to theory principle, with ASK_S(K,q)->QueryResult, Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal, Det(EVal,Gamma)->Determination as the three distinct operations; explicitly forbids Sat=ASK, Sat=Truth, and Determination=Truth as an invariant, motivated by the Handbook's model-based-reasoning distinction between obtaining predictions, comparing to observations, and drawing conclusions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Computationally Bounded Knowledge ... Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K) ... Explicit != Derivable != Available ... This is not UNKNOWN in the same sense as absence of representation. It is a computational boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-4 (section 5): distinguishes Cn_S(K) (all consequences) from Avail_S(K,B) (what a bounded reasoning process can actually compute), with Avail_S(K,B) subseteq Cn_S(K), giving a three-way distinction Explicit != Derivable != Available; a proposition can be derivable-but-unavailable, which is a computational-boundary phenomenon, explicitly NOT the same kind of UNKNOWN as absence of representation. Flagged as feeding the future Zero/Evaluation model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Epistemic Change as multiple mechanisms ... reject a single undifferentiated K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x). Instead ... Revision != Contraction != Update ... revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-5 (section 6): rejects a single undifferentiated transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x); requires distinguishing Revision(K_t,e)->K_{t+1} (correction/reorganization of a static-world epistemic state), Contraction(K_t,p)->K_{t+1} (withdrawal of a commitment), and Update(K_t,Delta W)->K_{t+1} (the represented world changed) as semantic categories (not necessarily three implementation services), following the Handbook's revision-vs-update distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement non-monotonic knowledge evolution ... Classical accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient ... p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} ... Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic ... someone could incorrectly interpret K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse.' It may instead be Correction or Retraction or World Update.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-6 (section 7): classical monotone accumulation K_t subseteq K_{t+1} is insufficient; the theory must permit p in K_t while p not in K_{t+1} (Knowledge evolution is not necessarily monotonic), grounded in the Handbook's nonmonotonic-reasoning treatment of withdrawable conclusions. Warns explicitly against misreading K_{t+1} not-supseteq K_t as 'knowledge got worse' -- it may instead be Correction, Retraction, or World Update.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Representation Adequacy ... pi: X -> Y ... x1 != x2 can nevertheless satisfy pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2) ... Adequacy(pi,Q) means the projection preserves every distinction required by question Q ... Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. I would now consider this a core KnowledgeOS theory principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-7 (section 8): formalizes Representation Adequacy for a projection pi:X->Y, defining the induced equivalence x1 ~_pi x2 iff pi(x1)=pi(x2), and Adequacy(pi,Q) meaning pi preserves every distinction required by question Q; integrates with existing Projection work into the sequence Structure -> Projection -> Induced Equivalence -> Information Loss -> Invariant Preservation -> Adequacy. Elevated to a core KnowledgeOS theory principle, grounded in the Handbook's qualitative-representation/abstraction treatment. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE -> promote.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'failure to derive' as a typed epistemic distinction ... U_rep, U_der, U_avail, U_evid, U_eval, U_scope ... We do not need to make these six values of one enum ... we should not flatten them. Instead EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) remains the better direction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 9 (feeding FR-3/FR-4): distinguishes six typed causes of epistemic failure-to-derive -- U_rep (not represented), U_der (not derivable under S), U_avail (derivable but resource-unavailable), U_evid (insufficient evidence), U_eval (evaluation cannot determine), U_scope (outside declared scope) -- explicitly refusing to flatten them into one enum, per prior FDE/Zero experiments, and reaffirming the structured EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) direction as better than a flat value set. Grounded in the Handbook's observation that incomplete reasoning and incomplete knowledge can have different causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Revision Lineage ... if p->q and p supports q, then removing p can invalidate the derivation of q. Therefore derived content should retain a dependency structure: Support(q)={p, p->q, ...} ... This is not merely provenance ... It is derivation dependency ... DerivationLineage as a candidate theory concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-8 (section 10): if p->q and p supports q, removing p can invalidate the derivation of q; derived content should retain a dependency structure Support(q) = {p, p->q, ...}, named DerivationLineage and distinguished from ordinary provenance (it is derivation dependency, stronger than provenance-of-origin), grounded in the Handbook's belief-revision discussion. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'revision is constrained, not uniquely determined' ... Constraints(delta) not=> Unique(delta) ... Semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established. This principle applies beyond revision: equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, policy semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 11 (general methodological principle): AGM-style material shows desirable rationality constraints do not determine a unique revision operator (Constraints(delta) does not imply Unique(delta)); generalized as 'semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established', explicitly extended beyond revision to equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, and policy semantics. Judged compatible with existing kernel discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Temporal Persistence as distinct from Knowledge ... An entity/state can persist because no terminating event has been represented, but that is not equivalent to knowing that it persists ... Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange not=> NoChange. This is important for our future delta.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-9 (section 12): persistence (an entity/state persisting because no terminating event has been represented) is distinct from knowing that it persists; states Persistence != Truth != Knowledge and NoKnownChange does not imply NoChange, drawn from the Handbook's Event Calculus inertia/release treatment; flagged as important for the future delta definition. Status: STRONG CANDIDATE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement temporal qualification ... p@t or p@[t1,t2] ... Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction ... Epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction. This is especially important for our recent cross-frame contradiction work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 13: proposes temporal qualification p@t or p@[t1,t2] (instants, intervals, granularity as distinct representation choices, per the Handbook) so Eval(p,t1) and Eval(p,t2) can legitimately differ without contradiction; states the principle 'epistemic validity may be temporally indexed; temporal disagreement is not automatically logical contradiction', flagged as important for the corpus's cross-frame contradiction work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement distributed evidence -- but not distributed knowledge logic ... E1 union E2 union E3 may jointly support a determination even when Det(E1)=U, Det(E2)=U, Det(E3)=U ... JointEvidence != sum IndividualDeterminations ... do not import epistemic logic's D_G, common knowledge, or agent semantics into the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-11 (section 14): union of individually-undetermined evidence sources (Det(E1)=Det(E2)=Det(E3)=U) may jointly support a determination, drawn from the Handbook's distributed-knowledge treatment; proposes the weaker KnowledgeOS principle JointEvidence != sum(IndividualDeterminations) and JointSupport(E_G,p|Gamma), while explicitly forbidding import of epistemic logic's distributed-knowledge operator D_G, common knowledge, or full agent semantics into the kernel. Status: CANDIDATE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Task Knowledge as a separate theoretical layer ... DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism ... PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput ... otherwise KnowledgeOS risks treating every reasoning process as generic.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-10 (section 15): drawing on the Handbook's Problem-Solving Method (PSM) material as highly DDD-compatible, proposes DomainKnowledge != TaskKnowledge != ReasoningMechanism, with PSM: Input -> ReasoningPattern -> TaskOutput, and a DDD interpretation chain BoundedContext -> DomainKnowledge -> Task -> PSM -> Reasoning -> Determination; motivated by the risk that KnowledgeOS otherwise treats every reasoning process as generic. Recorded as candidate theory structure, not kernel primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement model multiplicity as a determination concept ... M(K,Gamma) ... |M|=0 could indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics ... |M|=1 could indicate model-level uniqueness ... |M|>1 indicates underdetermination ... |M|=1 does not automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition ... ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination.
b_rows_sample.statement: FR-12 (section 16): defines M(K,Gamma) as the set of models compatible with current knowledge and context: |M|=0 may indicate inconsistency under the relevant model semantics, |M|=1 model-level uniqueness, |M|>1 underdetermination; explicit warning that |M|=1 does NOT automatically mean KnowledgeOS has determined the proposition (model space and reasoning capability still matter), yielding ModelUniqueness != KnowledgeDetermination. Status: RESEARCH CANDIDATE, upgraded to 'very strong candidate'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implement diagnosability as an evidence-quality property ... A useful observation/test is one that discriminates among competing hypotheses ... DiscriminativePower(e,H) ... this does not revive N_eff. Our previous negative result remains: PairwiseDistinguishability not=> FamilyComplexity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 17: proposes DiscriminativePower(e,H) as a candidate evidence-quality property (a useful observation/test discriminates among competing hypotheses, per the Handbook's model-based reasoning chapter), explicitly noting this does NOT revive the previously-rejected N_eff metric, and reaffirms the standing negative result PairwiseDistinguishability does not imply FamilyComplexity; final principle: evidence can be evaluated by the distinctions it preserves among admissible hypotheses.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The resulting KnowledgeOS theory structure ... Truth/World State -> Observation -> Evidence -> Representation (Explicit/Derived/Contextual) -> Reasoning S -> Evaluation Eval_c -> Determination -> Decision -> Action -> Observation' ... Orthogonal dimensions: Context, Time, Provenance, Authority, Scope, Computational Boundary ... And state change: K_t -> Revision / Contraction / World Update / New Observation / New Reasoning Capability -> K_t+1
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 19 assembles the whole review into one restructured theory diagram: a linear pipeline Truth/World-State -> Observation -> Evidence -> Representation(Explicit/Derived/Contextual) -> Reasoning-S -> Evaluation(Eval_c) -> Determination -> Decision -> Action -> Observation', six orthogonal dimensions (Context, Time, Provenance, Authority, Scope, Computational Boundary), and a five-way state-change fan-out from K_t (Revision, Contraction, World Update, New Observation, New Reasoning Capability) into K_t+1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If I reduce the entire book to the minimum theory contribution, I would make this the new KnowledgeOS epistemic law: Evidence is not directly Knowledge. More formally: E -> Rep -> Reason_S -> Eval_c -> Det, with Truth, Context, Time, Provenance, Authority remaining orthogonal dimensions. And knowledge evolution is not one operation: Revision != Contraction != WorldUpdate != Reasoning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 21, the review's single most-reduced claim, proposed as a new KnowledgeOS epistemic law: 'Evidence is not directly Knowledge', formalized as the chain E -> Rep -> Reason_S -> Eval_c -> Det with Truth/Context/Time/Provenance/Authority as orthogonal dimensions, and knowledge evolution decomposed as Revision != Contraction != WorldUpdate != Reasoning; judged to be what can actually be implemented into the theory now without violating existing epistemic discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not call this Theory v1.3 yet. Instead create a controlled research artifact: KR-HR -- KnowledgeOS Theory Integration from Handbook of Knowledge Representation ... FR-1-FR-7: eligible for theory promotion after corpus reconciliation ... FR-8-FR-10: strong candidates requiring one additional validation pass ... FR-11-FR-12: research candidates ... Contr / Zero / Sat / Equality / delta: remain open ... Kernel selection: unchanged.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommended status/governance discipline: explicitly declines to name this Theory v1.3, instead proposing the bounded research artifact KR-HR with graded eligibility (FR-1..FR-7 eligible for promotion after corpus reconciliation; FR-8..FR-10 strong candidates needing one more validation pass; FR-11..FR-12 research candidates), while Contr/Zero/Sat/Equality/delta remain open and kernel selection stays unchanged -- preserving the archaeology -> evidence -> determination -> ratification discipline.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Until now we have used Zero intuitively as 'the gap between where we are and where we need to be.' We now need to make that statement mathematically precise. The decisive test is: Can Zero(K,G,EC) be computed from the KnowledgeState? If yes, Zero becomes a genuine computational primitive of Knowledg
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 25D's decisive test: can Zero(K,G,EC) be computed from the KnowledgeState, making Zero a genuine computational primitive rather than an AI metaphor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A conventional system might define Delta=Target-Current. That is insufficient for KnowledgeOS. ... Nexus version known/3.69 known, Rollback verified/unknown, Firewall permitted/conflicting, Architecture approval/missing. There are four fundamentally different situations. Therefore Zero != simple sub
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the naive Delta=Target-Current model of Zero using a four-requirement worked example (known/unknown/conflicting/missing), establishing Zero≠simple subtraction — it must compare requirements against epistemic state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Let the goal be G. The goal induces a set of required knowledge conditions: R_G={r_1,r_2,...,r_n}. For Nexus migration ... r_1=CurrentVersionKnown ... r_7=GovernanceApprovalObtained. This is crucial: Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone. We need the Epistemic Contract that tells us what must
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge Requirement set R_G induced by a goal G (worked with seven Nexus-migration requirements r1-r7), establishing that Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone and requires an Epistemic Contract.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define EC_G=(R_G,Gamma_G) where R_G = required conditions; Gamma_G = rules determining sufficiency. So EC_G = what must be established + how sufficiency is judged. This gives Zero a formal input.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Epistemic Contract EC_G=(R_G,Γ_G) — required conditions plus sufficiency rules — as Zero's formal input.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For each requirement r_i, we evaluate its status against K_t. Define Sat(K_t,r_i). Initially I propose the following state set: S={Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable}. This is already much richer than Boolean logic.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a nine-value requirement-satisfaction status set (Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable), explicitly richer than Boolean logic.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Sat(K,r)=False. That could mean: we know it is false; we don't know; evidence conflicts; evidence is stale; evidence was invalidated; governance prohibits the action. These are operationally very different. Therefore Sat != Boolean.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues Sat≠Boolean: a bare False collapses six operationally distinct situations (known-false, unknown, conflicting, stale, invalidated, prohibited) into one indistinguishable value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We can define Z_i=Status(K_t,r_i,EC_G). Then Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i) | r_i in R_G}. This gives us a Zero vector. For example Z(K)=[Satisfied,Satisfied,Unknown,Insufficient,Conflicted,Satisfied,Missing]. Now Zero is computationally representable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i)} as a computationally representable 'Zero vector' of per-requirement statuses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Case A: No evidence exists: Evidence(r)=empty. Status: Unknown. Case B: Governance requires approval, and no approval exists. That is Missing. These are different. So I recommend Missing as a separate status where the requirement itself is an expected governed artifact/action.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Unknown (no evidence exists at all) from Missing (an expected governed artifact/action, such as an approval, that does not exist) as two different status values.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose current KnowledgeState contains A_1: NexusVersion=3.69, A_2: RepositoryCount=43, but nothing about rollback. Then Status(r_1)=Satisfied but Status(r_3)=Unknown. If Architecture Board approval is explicitly required and has not been issued: Status(r_7)=Missing. Therefore Zero(K)={r_3:Unknown,
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked Nexus example computing a concrete Zero(K)={r3:Unknown, r7:Missing} from partial knowledge state evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We can therefore define Zero(K,G,EC)=R_G \ Satisfied(K,R_G) but this is only a shorthand. The real result must retain why each requirement is not satisfied. So Zero={Requirement, Status, Evidence, Reason, Dependencies}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a shorthand set-difference definition of Zero (R_G minus satisfied requirements) into the fuller structured form Zero={Requirement,Status,Evidence,Reason,Dependencies}, retaining why each requirement is unsatisfied.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Zero item should look conceptually like: Requirement: RollbackVerified; Status: Unknown; SupportingEvidence: none; BlockingReason: no successful restore test; RequiredAction: perform restore test; DecisionCriticality: high. This is already implementable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a concrete implementable structured-Zero-item template with six fields (Requirement, Status, SupportingEvidence, BlockingReason, RequiredAction, DecisionCriticality).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_1 supports RollbackVerified=True. Is that enough? Not necessarily. The epistemic contract may require 2 independent tests. Or 1 test witnessed by a designated authority. Or Probability(success)>=0.99. Therefore Satisfied = ContractSpecific.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that satisfaction of a requirement is ContractSpecific — the same supporting evidence may or may not count as satisfied depending on the epistemic contract's own sufficiency rule (independent-test count, witness authority, or probability threshold).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We therefore need Satisfied(K,r,EC) which may invoke the appropriate reasoning model. For example Satisfied(K,r,EC)=RuleEngine(K,r,EC) or =StatisticalCriterion(K,r,EC) or =HumanAuthorization(K,r). This is another reason Zero must not contain one universal inference mechanism.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the satisfaction predicate Satisfied(K,r,EC) as potentially delegating to RuleEngine, StatisticalCriterion, or HumanAuthorization — reinforcing that Zero must not embed one universal inference mechanism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero should not calculate everything itself. Instead: Zero -> RequirementEvaluation -> AppropriateReasoningModel. ... Zero aggregates the results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Zero as an orchestrator that dispatches requirement evaluation to the appropriate reasoning model (Rules/Statistics/Authority) and aggregates results, rather than being an inference engine itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Operational Zero: Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) where W* is the target world state. Epistemic Zero: Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC) where K*_EC is the knowledge required by the epistemic contract. These are fundamentally different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally splits Operational Zero Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) from Epistemic Zero Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC), reaffirming the two are fundamentally different quantities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Target: Nexus Pro running in target environment. Current world: Nexus OSS 3.69 running. Operational gap: Z_W>0. But suppose Target architecture known, Current version known, Backup status unknown, Firewall status unknown, Approval missing. Then Z_K>0. Even if an engineer knows exactly how to perform
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing Z_K (epistemic gap) can independently block execution even when the operational how-to is fully known, illustrating Z_W and Z_K as genuinely separate blocking gaps.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I recommend Zero=(Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision) at the conceptual level. Z_world: What differs in reality? Z_knowledge: What required facts are unknown/uncertain? Z_governance: What required approvals/rules are missing? Z_decision: What prevents a defensible decision? This is much
a_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes Zero into four conceptual dimensions (Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision), each answering a distinct question, stronger than a single scalar distance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Z_knowledge=5 and Z_governance=1. Can we say Zero=6? No. The six missing items are not necessarily comparable. One missing governance approval could be more blocking than five low-priority informational gaps. Therefore Zero is primarily a structured object, not a scalar.
a_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample against summing dimension counts into a scalar Zero=6: a single governance gap can outweigh five informational gaps in blocking severity, so Zero must remain primarily a structured object, not a scalar.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Once the structured Zero exists, we may calculate: GapCount. Or CriticalGapCount. Or WeightedGapScore. Or ContractCoverage. For example Coverage(K) = satisfied required conditions / total required conditions. But these are projections of Zero, not Zero itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four derivable scalar projections of the structured Zero object (GapCount, CriticalGapCount, WeightedGapScore, ContractCoverage), explicitly distinguished as projections, not Zero itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Each requirement can have Criticality(r) such as {Critical,High,Medium,Low}. But again, we should be careful with arbitrary scores. A critical requirement might be RollbackVerified. If Status=Unknown, then migration could be blocked regardless of all other results. This gives us BlockingCondition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces per-requirement Criticality with a caution against arbitrary scoring, deriving the concept of a BlockingCondition — a single unresolved critical requirement that blocks regardless of all other results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A gap is an absence or deficiency in a Knowledge State relative to what is needed for a specific purpose, context, or decision ... Gap \neq Conflict ... Gap = Absence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Gap as distinct from Conflict (absence/deficiency vs. tension/incompatibility) with six gap types (MissingDimension, UnknownValue, MissingEvidence, InsufficientEvidence, StaleKnowledge, ContextualGap) and a Gap structure (Type,Target,Severity,Context,Status,tau); initially equates Gap with Absence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gap \neq Absence. Gap = Insufficiency relative to a requirement ... R(P,C,t) = KnowledgeRequirements(P,C,t) ... Gap(K,P,C,t) iff K not-models R(P,C,t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Gap=Absence (too narrow -- insufficient evidence or stale knowledge is not absence) to Gap=Insufficiency-relative-to-a-requirement: introduces R(P,C,t) as the knowledge requirements generated by purpose/context/time, and defines Gap(K,P,C,t) iff K does not entail/satisfy R(P,C,t) -- the same knowledge can be sufficient for one purpose and gappy for another (e.g. Nexus.Version=3.69 suffices for 'what version' but not 'can it be safely migrated').

Concludes the argument actually dropped across these forms is G, not EC -- EC survives in five of the six forms -- so the original G-01 premise is REFUTED, not merely too strong, and was asking about the wrong argument.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A search defect found first, and it changes the count ... A glyph-only search returns 1 file of 11 and 2 occurrences of 28 — a 93% miss.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds the corpus writes the symbol Omega two ways (Unicode glyph Omega and LaTeX \Omega): across steps 231-267 there are 28 total occurrences in 11 of 40 files, but a glyph-only search finds only 2 occurrences in 1 file -- a 93% miss rate -- establishing that any symbol sweep for this corpus must cover both notations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ω Sense Inventory — FIVE senses ... (Ω-1 ontology, Ω-2 observation, Ω-3 transition arg, Ω-4 state measure space, Ω-5 generic placeholder)
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconstructs five distinct in-window Omega senses with birth documents and identity status: Omega-1 'ontology' (Omega=domain ontology/rules, born 025k L53 2026-08-28 09:39, status CONTINUOUS within its family then RE-FOUNDED AWAY at 031); Omega-2 'observation' (Omega:W->O, defined 031 SS31.18 2026-08-28 10:22 as the observation mechanism, status IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED though byte-identical in type to 031); Omega-3 'transition arg' (untyped 4th argument of delta_K(K_t,o_t,rho_t,Omega_t), born step-016 L1993 2026-08-27 16:00, the OLDEST readable Omega, IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED, its own sources say the signature is unresolved); Omega-4 'state measure space' (Omega=K, the sample space IS the knowledge-state space, born 238 L16 during the R1 measure-theory phase, EXPLICITLY_REDEFINED then abandoned as a 'temptation'); Omega-5 'generic placeholder' (borrowed textbook notation for algebra/measurement/probability-space conventions, never a KnowledgeOS object, classified HOMONYM).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ⛔ Correction to my own prior finding ... Net: 6 → 5 senses, with one previously invisible collision inside a single document.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the investigation's own prior claim (09-EVIDENCE-LOG.md SS5) that Omega has six mutually incompatible meanings: that count over-counted Omega-4 across three retrospective-citation sites as three separate senses, under-attributed Omega:W->O's definitional source (031 SS31.18, two days before the 251 citation), and missed both Omega-1 (the 025-series ontology sense, co-occurring 300 lines from Omega:W->O in the same document step_251) and Omega-5 (236's explicit 'a set of operations' gloss). Net correction: 6 senses collapses to 5, revealing a previously invisible collision (Omega-1 and Omega-2 coexisting unremarked within a single document, step_251).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ω_a / Ω_b / Ω_c — an explicit split record whose terms are never defined [later WITHDRAWN, see §12.1] ... The role survived as an invariant; whether the SYMBOL continued to denote it is a separate question the corpus does not answer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records step_238's assertion that Omega diverged into three roles (Omega_a->IdealState/contract, Omega_b->dropped, Omega_c->complement principle => invariant I-7: X_t != Observed(X_t)) with no document (in the initially searched forms) defining the three terms individually; notes the ROLE carried by Omega_c demonstrably survives as invariant I-7 with the same semantics as Omega:W->O, but the corpus never states that the SYMBOL Omega_c became Omega:W->O -- recorded as IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED, not continuity. (This claim about Omega_a/b/c being undefined is itself later withdrawn in section 12.1 of the same file upon a wider evidence sweep.)

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4. Ω : W → O — located, typed, and its inheritance tested ... retained / weakened / altered / abandoned? RETAINED, unchanged, at the one site that carries it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces Omega:W->O to its definitional source (031 SS31.18 L598, boxed, 2026-08-28 10:22:51, with W_t='the relevant real-world state' and O_t=Obs(W_t) the partial observation) and tests inheritance: only step_251 (18:36, two days later) carries the byte-identical W->O signature, and it does so via an unattributed citation to 'the corpus' with no step number or explicit equivalence claim -- every other in-window Omega has a different or absent type. Status: RETAINED unchanged at the one site that carries it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 5. Four histories, kept separate (Conceptual / Mathematical / Operational / Governance) ... A later mathematical redefinition has not overwritten an earlier conceptual record here — because there was never a redefinition. There were independent definitions that never met.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four independent histories for Omega: Conceptual (four unrelated referents -- derivation rule-set, world-to-observation mechanism, an unnamed fourth transition argument, and the space of possible knowledge states -- with no conceptual thread connecting them); Mathematical (one function W->O, one rule set, one measure-space carrier, one untyped argument, one borrowed placeholder -- only Omega-2 has a definitionally stated signature); Operational (Omega-1 consumed by Update/Derive, Omega-3 by delta_K, Omega-2 never consumed by any operation in the window, Omega-4 demoted from foundation to regime to 'temptation', Omega-5 never operational); Governance/history (R1, Omega-4's home, is classified a 'failed direction' with ALT-01 recorded -- but this claim of 'no governance act on Omega itself' is later withdrawn in section 12.2). Concludes there was never a redefinition overwriting an earlier record -- these were independent definitions that never met.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 6. Re-foundings — one explicit alignment, and it is the whole finding ... The symbol Ω crossed re-founding #1 and was re-used for a different object. Silently.
b_rows_sample.statement: Checks Omega's alignment against five known corpus re-foundings, finding only one decisive alignment: re-founding #1 (031, 'drops the 025 apparatus') explicitly drops the Omega-1=domain-ontology apparatus and, in the same document 43 minutes later, defines Omega:W->O as the observation mechanism, mentioning '025', 'domain ontology' or Update(K,E,Omega,EC) zero times. Re-foundings #2/#3/#5 show no Omega evidence; re-founding #4 (262, K=(A,R)) shows no alignment since Omega had already gone dark 51 minutes earlier; a shared classification with tau:SxC->S (Step 204) as sibling 'family' rows is explicitly recorded as classification only, not shared identity. Concludes the symbol Omega crossed re-founding #1 and was silently re-used for a different object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 7. G-19 not used ... no Ω sense was preferred because it makes the K model work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly records that no primary source connects the G-19 falsification result to any Omega sense, and no Omega sense was adjudicated or preferred on the grounds that it makes the K model work -- an independence discipline note.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 8. Identity matrix — all ten pairs ... Not one pair of the ten is supported as the same object by any corpus evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Builds a complete ten-pair identity matrix over the five senses: Omega-1xOmega-2 HOMONYM (explicit, 43 minutes apart, type-incompatible, coexisting unremarked 300 lines apart in step_251); Omega-2xOmega-3 DISTINCT by explicit differentiation (step-016 separately names Obs(X_t,S_t) and a different fourth argument Omega_t in the same boxed formula); Omega-1xOmega-4, Omega-1xOmega-5, Omega-2xOmega-4, Omega-2xOmega-5 DISTINCT by type; Omega-1xOmega-3, Omega-3xOmega-4, Omega-3xOmega-5 UNDECIDABLE (Omega-3 untyped, sources say so); Omega-4xOmega-5 POSSIBLE SAME OBJECT-identity-unwitnessed (both measure-theoretic sample-space notation, but Omega-4 commits to Omega=K while Omega-5 is a placeholder). Tally: 1 HOMONYM, 1 DISTINCT-by-differentiation, 4 DISTINCT-by-type, 3 UNDECIDABLE, 1 POSSIBLE-SAME-UNWITNESSED, 0 SAME OBJECT -- not one of the ten pairs is supported as the same object by any corpus evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 9. Mandatory adversarial check — both directions ... The corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs a two-directional adversarial evidence check: (A) searching for evidence that senses ARE one continuous object -- no identifying statement, rename/supersession/retirement record, or type bridge found, so results are recorded IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED rather than assumed distinct; (B) searching for evidence senses ARE distinct -- finds two incompatible explicit definitions (025k vs 031, 43 minutes apart, neither citing the other), one document (step-016) naming the observation function Obs while using Omega for a different argument, and step_238's own explicit 'Same word != Same concept' DDD-lesson collision-marking rule (applied there to Zero and Lord). The self-referential finding: step_238 states this exact discipline as a lesson, applies it to Zero and Lord, and in the same document uses Omega in three different senses without applying the lesson to Omega itself -- the corpus had the instrument and did not turn it on itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 10. Findings G22-1 through G22-8
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues eight findings: G22-1 (CRITICAL) Omega-1xOmega-2 is a HOMONYM on explicit definitional evidence, born 43 minutes apart across re-founding #1, neither citing the other; G22-2 (CRITICAL) step_251 carries both senses simultaneously 300 lines apart and never notices, the same document G-03's Omega/EC sub-family classification rests on; G22-3 (HIGH, corrective) five senses not six, correcting an over-split of Omega-4 and a missed Omega-1/Omega-5; G22-4 (CRITICAL, method) a glyph-only search misses 93% of Omega occurrences in this window; G22-5 (HIGH) Omega-3 is the oldest readable Omega (step-016, 2026-08-27) and untyped at birth with a second undefined argument rho_t alongside it; G22-6 (UNRESOLVED, HIGH) the Omega_a/b/c split is asserted with three named roles and zero types; G22-7 (UNRESOLVED, MEDIUM) no governance act touches Omega -- rename/supersession/retirement/collision record absent; G22-8 (MEDIUM) step_238 states 'Same word != Same concept' as a DDD lesson, applies it to Zero and Lord, yet itself uses Omega in three senses in the same document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 11. Scope discipline ... Ω-4's own sources call it a 'failed direction' and a 'temptation' — that is their classification, recorded, not adopted. ... Firewall: brainstorming/three_model_convergence/ was not opened
b_rows_sample.statement: Scopes the investigation: no sense is preferred, merged, repaired or retired; Omega-4's own sources' self-classification as a 'failed direction'/'temptation' is recorded, not adopted as the investigation's own judgment; three documents outside the 231-267 window were opened solely to type a symbol used inside it, importing no other content. Discloses the standing firewall: brainstorming/three_model_convergence/ was not opened, read, grepped or cited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.1 ⛔ Ω_a / Ω_b / Ω_c ARE defined — two days before 238 cites them ... 238 reports as settled what its source recorded as unresolved, with no derivation shown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the earlier §3 claim: a wider evidence sweep (3,108 files, 493 containing Omega) finds Omega_a/Omega_b/Omega_c ARE defined, two days before step_238 cites them, in combine-prompt-4 (2026-08-28 15:01:40): Omega-a=ideal reference->Ideal State->Epistemic Contract, Omega-b=unboundedness->dropped, Omega-c=whole-space observation->unresolved. The miss was a notation-form defect (searched subscript \Omega_a rather than the corpus's dominant hyphenated Omega-a form), yielding the methodological correction that symbol sweeps must cover both subscript and hyphen forms. Also finds step_238 changed Omega-c's fate from 'unresolved' (source) to 'complement principle -> invariant I-7' with no derivation shown, and that two downstream records disagree on where Omega-c went (DISPLACED-no-host per combine-prompt-4/lord-omega-analysis vs TRANSFORMED-into-its-complement per 238/phase-2d-closure), recorded as unreconciled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.2 ⛔ A governance ruling on Ω does exist ... Ω is ruled historical-only and excluded from the final ubiquitous language, on a reconstructed lineage basis ... Three of the five in-window senses are outside the scope of the only ruling that exists.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the earlier §5 claim that no governance act touches Omega: finds GN-09 (governance-notes.md L67, an 'Omega terminology ruling' -- Omega belongs to theory/history, not the final ubiquitous language, retained in the discovery record to explain the architecture's evolution), D-R27 (A3-definition-register.md L56, ruling Omega 'historical term only' and decomposing Omega-a->EC, Omega-b bounded away, Omega-c->X_t per GN-09, marked RECONSTRUCTED lineage ruling), and OQ-6 (Omega-b's drop recorded as an open record gap, 'dropped by disuse, no act'). Notes the corrected governance line rules Omega historical-only and excluded from the final ubiquitous language on a reconstructed-lineage basis, but this ruling governs only the Omega-a/b/c decomposition -- it does not mention Omega-1 (domain ontology), Omega-2 (Omega:W->O) or Omega-3 (delta_K's argument), leaving three of the five in-window senses outside the only ruling that exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.3 ⛔ The corpus had already registered the collision — and I re-derived it ... This is the G-19 pattern again, and this time I am inside it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds the corpus's verification lane had already registered the Omega overload eleven days earlier: TG-15 (THEORY-GAP-REGISTER.md L39, 2026-08-30 20:51) states 'Omega carries >=4 global senses, two of them foundational and opposite in direction... OPEN -- NEW, and the most dangerous naming collision found'; C-06 (11-CONTRADICTION-REGISTRY.md L17, 2026-08-30 21:16) states 'Omega = Knowledge Space vs Omega:W->O... TRUE CONTRADICTION... Unregistered by every prior pass.' Explicitly names this as a repeat of the G-19 pattern (a claimed absence was actually already executed/registered elsewhere) -- this time the investigation itself is inside that pattern. Notes what survives as genuinely new: TG-15's four senses (sample space, Knowledge Space, observation function, residual possibilities) do not include Omega-1 (domain ontology/rules, 025k L53), so the Omega-1 x Omega-2 homonym, its 43-minute interval, and its coincidence with re-founding #1 remain unrecorded elsewhere in the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.4 A sixth sense, out of window — and it is the other half of C-06 ... Ω-7 Knowledge Space ... Zero(K_t) = Ω \ Represented(K_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds a sixth/out-of-window sense Omega-7 'Knowledge Space' (from a 2026-08-26 Zero-lens research-synthesis document and three further files: Zero(K_t)=Omega\Represented(K_t), Omega as the infinite knowledge space of which any K_t is a partial projection). Notes Omega-7 is C-06's first (Knowledge-Space) term, does not occur in the 231-267 window, but is the sense the corpus itself judged most dangerous, and is the direct ancestor of Omega-a ('ideal reference'), making it upstream of the whole Omega_a/b/c decomposition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.5 An attribution in an independent verification that does not reproduce ... Two of the four Ω-origin attributions in that sentence do not reproduce. ... A wrong citation is not weak evidence for the identity — it is no evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Checks a downstream verification claim (TV-F-022-024) attributing four Omega-overload origin sites (step-007, step-008, step-016 SS54, step-017) and finds two do not reproduce at source: the cited formula F(K0,H,rho,Omega) does not occur anywhere in the universe (step-016 SS54 actually contains two separate boxed formulas, K(t)=Fold(...) and delta_K(K_t,o_t,rho_t,Omega_t), which the citation conflates); the claimed gloss 'Omega=ontology' in step-016 is unsupported (step-016 has exactly one Omega with no gloss); and step-017 contains ZERO Omega occurrences of either spelling. Concludes a wrong citation is not weak evidence for an identity claim but no evidence at all, and that adopting it would have wrongly made Omega-1 x Omega-3 read as SAME OBJECT on nothing at all -- so Omega-1 x Omega-3 stays UNDECIDABLE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.6 Ω after the window — G-11 is far larger than recorded ... Ω_K = the set of legitimate kernel operations ... Kṛṣṇa ≡ Ω: explicitly REJECTED
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds Omega's post-window (steps 268-292) footprint is far larger than previously recorded: 171 files, 64 containing Omega, 290 line-occurrences, becoming central to the Gita lane (step_286) with at least three further readings -- Omega=Sanjaya=observation capability (Omega-2 revived, connecting to the B0050 sanjaya-observation-layer object, corpus-native per the reviewer), Omega=epistemic horizon/infinite Knowledge Space with K_t proper-subset-of Omega (Omega-7 revived), and Omega_K=the set of legitimate kernel operations (Omega-5's operation-set reading, now promoted to a genuine KnowledgeOS object) -- while Krsna=Omega is explicitly REJECTED as a 'rejected metaphysical projection'. Concludes the two senses C-06 calls a TRUE CONTRADICTION are both live again after step 285, unreconciled, and G-11 must be re-scoped from 'Omega and EC reappear at step 282' to 'Omega re-enters across 64 files in at least three senses, two ruled contradictory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.7 Convergent corroboration of the 2026-08-24 origin ... Two independent passes, same two files of 92 dated that day, same characterisation. The G-21 gate verdict is unchanged and now double-sourced.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that this investigation's independent identification of Omega's origin files (2026-08-24) matches the corpus's own archaeology (AF-003, phase-archaeology-findings.md, 2026-08-28 17:35: 'Omega first appears 2026-08-24 in kernel lens docs as the ambient space of typed/Bayesian models -- one day before phase_measure_theory opens; the measure-theory crisis inherited Omega, it did not coin it') exactly -- two independent passes agreeing on the same two files (of 92 dated that day) and the same characterization, leaving the pre-existing G-21 gate verdict unchanged but now double-sourced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 12.8 Net effect on the disposition (before/after table)
b_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the net effect of the section-12 evidence sweep in a before/after table: in-window senses unchanged at 5; out-of-window senses grow from 1 to 2 (adding Omega-7); Omega_a/b/c goes from 'never defined' to defined 08-28 15:01 with 238 having altered Omega-c's recorded fate; governance goes from 'no act' to GN-09+D-R27 found (though not covering Omega-1/2/3); prior art on the collision goes from 'none found' to TG-15 and C-06 found; the Omega-1xOmega-2 HOMONYM finding remains STILL NEW since Omega-1 appears in none of TG-15's four senses; Omega-1xOmega-3 remains UNDECIDABLE, now with a refuted attribution attached; the G-21 gate remains open with its constraint unchanged, now double-sourced.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §1 · Population ... 44 of the 55 are step_286 — one step number ... ONE evidential lineage, not 44 confirmations. ... The two 'intervals' are not sequential — they overlap by ~44 hours ... Step numbers imply sequence; the chronology shows parallel lanes.
a_rows_sample.statement: Censuses Omega in steps 269-291: 168 files, 55 containing Omega, 293 total occurrences, of which 44 cluster in a single step (s286) written within one continuous 08-31/09-01 Gita-thread session -- explicitly weighted as ONE independent evidential lineage rather than 44 separate confirmations. Discovers the '269-291' and '231-267' windows are NOT sequential: the last Omega occurrence in the 231-267 window (s266, 2026-08-30 19:54:50) comes AFTER the first Omega occurrence in the 269-291 window (s286, 2026-08-28 23:52:31) -- the later-numbered window begins 1 day 20 hours before the earlier-numbered window ends, proving step numbers do not imply chronological sequence and the two ranges represent parallel, not sequential, lanes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §2, §6 · The Ω objects in this interval, with their definitional sources (Ω-A Sañjaya/observation, Ω-B epistemic horizon, Ω-C Ω_K kernel operations, Ω-D integration/element domain) ... Ω-D contains a type error inside one file
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four live post-267 Omega senses with verbatim sources: Omega-A 'Sanjaya/observation' (08-31, boxed Omega:W->O, described as 'recovered', citing D285-6); Omega-B 'epistemic horizon' (09-01, boxed Omega=epistemic horizon, explicitly rejecting both Omega=God and Omega=K as 'unjustified architectural identities'); Omega-C 'Omega_K kernel operations' (09-01, boxed K=(K_t,Omega_K) later K=(K_t,Omega_K,I), Omega_K='legitimate/permitted kernel operations'); Omega-D 'integration/element domain' (08-28, appearing as both a measure space and a set of knowledge states). Finds an internal type error within Omega-D's own single source document: one line integrates K_t OVER Omega (making K_t a function on Omega) while another quantifies 'for all K in Omega' (making K an element of Omega) -- K cannot be both; recorded, not repaired.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §5 · Three-level identity test ... does the horizon document mention Sañjaya? 0 times. does the Sañjaya document mention horizon? 0 times. ... a_rows_sample.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

Lord Lens (Ω): Represents the total, unbounded, and potentially infinite knowledge space. ... It is not a part of the system but a philosophical anchor ... a_rows_sample.anchor: §1–4 · The 025→026 boundary, object by object — and my G-12 headline qualified ... The concepts did not stop. They de-formalised. ... sufficiency 73% ... satisfaction 45% ... contract 40% ... The NOTATION was lost. The CONCEPTS ran on through 45–73% of the interval.

b_rows_sample.statement: Formally withdraws the corpus's own '07-THEORYSTATE-CHRONICLE.md' record of five re-foundings (031, 183-pre, 230, 262, 273), revising each label: 031's 'INDEPENDENT_REFOUNDING (drops the 025 apparatus)' is corrected -- 031 itself says it continues Steps 1-30; it is actually 026 that drops the apparatus while declaring continuity, the opposite framing; 183-pre's 'EXPLICIT_REPLACEMENT (pruning)' is downgraded to SELECTIVE_REJECTION since it affirms alignment and rejects only a named subset; 230's 'UNWITNESSED' becomes REDUCTION since it explicitly presupposes the existing architecture; 262's 'EXPLICIT_REPLACEMENT' becomes CORRECTION since it names its predecessor and corrects one specific conclusion; 273 unchanged. Concludes (with G-25 having already removed the sixth candidate) this reconstruction removes the whole 're-founding' CONCEPT itself, replacing five separate events with one general mechanism: in this corpus, apparatus is lost across declared continuities -- authors say they continue and mean it, but the objects do not travel with the declaration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §16 · The ten questions Q1–Q10 (full table)
b_rows_sample.statement: Answers ten structured research questions about the interval: Q1 the 025 apparatus did not cross (0 in 265 files, cited once as a table row 41 seconds after continuity was declared); Q2 Omega/tau/K_t/Zero/EC/Delta_t/Gamma/Req are all born inside the interval (inherited from nothing) while Determination is genuinely inherited from a governance lane; Q3 the whole evaluation/satisfaction family was independently re-derived, clearest case Determination's 155a formalization vs Det_r; Q4 no definition inside the interval completes an earlier one -- all distributed-completeness successes cross OUT of the interval; Q5 apparent gaps (Omega:W->O, EvalReq's codomain-name, S_sat) were all resolved from OUTSIDE the interval; Q6 genuine type changes found in Update (10 signatures), Omega (5 senses), Sat (4 codomains); Q7 homonyms/identity-unwitnessed cases include Omega x5, Update x10, Gamma, Determination (governance vs mathematical), and step-026 itself (two documents, one number, a day apart); Q8 K-formulation origins traced (K_t s028; K_v1 7-tuple at 031; K_v2 6-tuple only in an s155-156 recovery doc quoting 'the earlier model'; K_v3 (A,R) from outside the interval); Q9 per-object silence/activity counts (Sat and EvalReq: ZERO occurrences in the entire interval); Q10 three carry-forward lessons: declared continuity != transmitted apparatus, the terminal staircase pattern, and the inherited codomain defect across three eras.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §18 · Terminal classification (Ω class E, Sat/EvalReq class C, Determination class E, Update class E, K_t class B, the interval itself class A structural)
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues terminal classifications: Omega = class E (OBJECT IDENTITY UNRESOLVED, five senses, 0 of 10 pairs same, per G-22); Sat/EvalReq = class C (COMPETING COMPLETE DEFINITIONS, four codomains, two indexing strategies, per G-25, though entirely absent from this interval); Determination = class E (IDENTITY UNRESOLVED across governance birth, mathematical formalization, and Det_r, no citation between any pair); Update/transition = class E (10 signatures, no stated relation); K_t = class B (complete through multiple sources, but those sources are outside the interval); the interval itself = class A, COMPLETE HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION (structural) -- births, silences, returns and deaths now fully mapped mechanically for 9 objects over 265 files.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §14 · Negative history ... Not found: Sat, Sat_c, EvalReq, EvalRequirement, R_G, Γ_G, EC_G, Derive(H,Ω,EC), ContractSpecific, EpistemicContract. ⇒ Recorded DEFINED ELSEWHERE ... not GENUINE CORPUS GAP. Det_r's body remains FIREWALL-LIMITED
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a negative-history search across all 265 files (both spellings, word-bounded, first-match step extraction) confirming zero occurrences of ten named objects (Sat, Sat_c, EvalReq, EvalRequirement, R_G, Gamma_G, EC_G, Derive(H,Omega,EC), ContractSpecific, EpistemicContract). Correctly classifies these as DEFINED ELSEWHERE (they exist before the interval at 023/025 and after it at 09-02/09-06) rather than GENUINE CORPUS GAP, per the programme's own discipline against declaring absence-within-a-bounded-window a true gap. Det_r's body remains classified FIREWALL-LIMITED (97% of occurrences excluded). Confirms firewall honoured, nothing canonicalized, no definition selected, all versions preserved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Concludes a gap was opened for an object the corpus had already defined three days earlier, then closed by 'recovering' it -- the corpus does not record this as a loss, it records it as a discovery. Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §1–4 · The 025→026 boundary, object by object — and my G-12 headline qualified ... The concepts did not stop. They de-formalised. ... sufficiency 73% ... satisfaction 45% ... contract 40% ... The NOTATION was lost. The CONCEPTS ran on through 45–73% of the interval.
b_rows_sample.statement: Qualifies the prior G-12 finding that the 025 apparatus 'vanishes' at step 026: while all formal 025 SYMBOLS score exactly 0 across 265 files (confirmed true), a census of the underlying 025-era CONCEPTS in prose form finds sufficiency at 73% (193/265 files), satisfaction at 45% (120/265), contract at 40% (107/265), gap at 20%, acceptance criterion at 2%, while the specific phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0. Concludes the NOTATION was lost but the CONCEPTS ran on informally through 45-73% of the interval -- the earlier headline ('the apparatus vanishes') is true only of formal notation, not of underlying concepts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: And precisely which form survived ... Of 241 satisf* occurrences sampled: 83 in technical context, 158 prose. ... What survived is satisfaction as a PREDICATE. What was lost is satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Samples 241 'satisf*' occurrences (83 technical, 158 prose) and verifies at ten specific steps (s070,079,081,086,091,092,095,097,098,101) that the surviving technical usage is uniformly an unformalised predicate ('the rule is satisfied', 'invariants remain satisfied') rather than the 025-series typed function Satisfied(K,r,EC) with three typed arguments and a result space S(9->10->11). Concludes precisely what survived was satisfaction AS A PREDICATE; what was lost was satisfaction as a TYPED FUNCTION WITH A RESULT SPACE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An interpretation, marked as such ... consistent with — and would explain — the four divergent Sat codomains found in G-25 ... nothing carried a result space through the interval, so each later lane supplied its own. ⛔ Recorded as [PROPOSED], not as a cause.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, explicitly marked as an unproven interpretation (not a corpus-stated cause), that the loss of a shared result space during the interval would explain why G-25 later found four mutually non-citing Sat codomains (S 9-11, V_Sat 3, S_sat 4, S_sat variant): each later lane, lacking an inherited result space, supplied its own. Notes this hypothesis is recorded as [PROPOSED] rather than established, citing a cautionary precedent -- a previously withdrawn batch-003 claim ('the semantics-bearing argument always disappears') that failed for exactly the same overreach.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §6 · Distributed completeness — the corrected classification ... EvalReq is the only 025-era object whose concept as well as its notation leaves the interval. That singles it out, and it is the one object G-25 found still untyped at 09-06.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provides a corrected four-row classification: '025 apparatus vanishes at 026' is corrected from PARTIALLY-EVIDENCED to DE-FORMALISED (symbols 0, concepts 45-73%); 'Sat is absent from 026-268' stands for the FUNCTION but is FALSE for the underlying CONCEPT (0 vs 120 files); 'EvalReq is absent' stands fully, both notation and concept (even the phrase 'requirement evaluation' scores 0/265); 'Omega-B has no type' is REFUTED (excluded by design, per S14). Concludes EvalReq is uniquely the only 025-era object whose CONCEPT, not merely its notation, actually leaves the interval -- and it is the same object G-25 separately found still untyped as late as 09-06.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §8, §12 · Identity and DDD — EC is the interval's worst case ... Three ECs, three arities, three bounded contexts, zero cross-references ... Verdict: HOMONYM ×3, IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies EC as a triple homonym with zero cross-references between any pair: EC=EpistemicClaim (s032, 11-tuple, 'the atomic unit of KnowledgeOS'); EC=engineering change (s117, 8-tuple, 'a test object' in a traceability experiment); EC=EpistemicContract (025-series, (R_G,Gamma_G) shape, 0 occurrences in steps 026-154). Classifies this as HOMONYM x3 with IDENTITY UNWITNESSED between every pair, noting it is the same shape of finding as Determination (governance vs mathematical vs Det_r) and Gamma (four senses), already recorded elsewhere in this programme.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §7 · Mathematical typing across the interval (PROVEN: Ω-2, K_v0, K_v1, EC-claim, Γ_A, EC-engchange; UNKNOWN: Zero never defined, Δ_t only α_t defined, Ω_t unresolved, Update 10 signatures) ... No promotion of TYPE-CONSTRAINED or INFERRED to PROVEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Audits mathematical typing status across the interval: PROVEN objects include Omega-2 (W->O), K_v0 (9-tuple, s028), K_v1 (7-tuple, s031), EC-claim (11-tuple, s032), Gamma_A (4-tuple, s053), EC-engchange (8-tuple, s117); UNKNOWN status objects include Zero (never defined anywhere in 265 files), Delta_t (one occurrence, whose 'where' clause defines only a sub-component alpha_t, not Delta_t itself), Omega_t as an argument of delta_K (signature declared unresolved by its own cited sources), and Update (10 unrelated signatures).
