a_rows_sample.anchor: Established (TV-F-007/008): V!=empty under interpretation (M0/M1) - system is a liveness-free schema over >=12 uninterpreted predicates - fresh IDs mandatory (5x I_1, 6 IDs for Unknown!=False, swapped registries).
a_rows_sample.statement: Records three prior established findings (TV-F-007/008) that this plan builds on: the state space is non-empty under interpretation (models M0/M1); the system is a liveness-free schema over at least 12 uninterpreted predicates; and fresh IDs are mandatory because of naming collisions found in the source corpus -- five separate uses of the label 'I_1', six different IDs all covering the 'Unknown != False' family, and at least one case of swapped registries.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 1 -- Fresh-ID consolidated catalogue ... Mint KI-nnn for every distinct invariant statement across the >=10 registries (~130 statements) ... Dedup rule: semantic near-duplicates grouped, never merged -- the group is the object.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 1 mints a fresh KI-nnn identifier for every distinct invariant statement found across at least 10 separate corpus registries (roughly 130 statements total), recording per row: the KI-ID, the canonical verbatim-anchored statement, all source IDs and locations, its semantic-duplicate group, its layer (assigned in Step 2), its modal strength (MUST/SHOULD as found, both recorded where an invariant carries dual strength, e.g. K5), and its status from prior A5/TV-F verdicts where already touched. States a deduplication rule: semantic near-duplicates are grouped, never merged into one -- the group itself, not a single representative, is treated as the object of record.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 2 -- Layer classification (per 1600 section13's demand to distinguish) Each KI classified: DEFINITIONAL ... NORMATIVE-EPISTEMIC ... NORMATIVE-GOVERNANCE (K1-K7, authority family) ... METHODOLOGICAL (I-8, no-assertion-without-evidence) ... ARCHITECTURAL/OPERATIONAL ... EMPIRICAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 2 classifies every consolidated invariant (KI) into one of six layers per an earlier document's ('1600 section 13') demand: DEFINITIONAL (holds by construction of the event-log/state-machinery, e.g. several of the '197' conservation laws), NORMATIVE-EPISTEMIC (the Unknown != False family), NORMATIVE-GOVERNANCE (the K1-K7 authority family), METHODOLOGICAL (e.g. I-8, no-assertion-without-evidence), ARCHITECTURAL/OPERATIONAL (test-assertion shaped), and EMPIRICAL (calibration-type); explicitly reuses a corpus-native four-constraint-kind scheme (cited as '162') as the template for this classification rather than inventing a new one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 3 -- Per-layer satisfiability at intended semantics ... exhibit a model or a minimal unsatisfiable subset ... Expected hard spots: governance layer under multi-authority (needs the precedence device); epistemic layer's Conflicted-exit (needs adjudication signature)
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 3 requires, for each layer, once its predicates receive interpretations (from prior V2/V3 outcomes plus governance devices), exhibiting either a satisfying model or a minimal unsatisfiable subset, extending the baseline models M0/M1 per layer; names three expected hard spots in advance: the governance layer under multi-authority conditions (needing a precedence device), the epistemic layer's Conflicted-exit case (needing an adjudication signature), and anything consuming the terms 'authoritative'/'material'/'governed' (needing formal definitions for these terms).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 4 -- Independence/redundancy analysis ... Output: a minimal generating subset per layer -- PROPOSED, never a deletion of the others.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 4 analyzes, within each layer, which KIs are logically implied by others (candidate example: several '048' items follow from the event-log construction plus provenance conservation) versus which are independent axioms; the output is a minimal generating subset per layer, explicitly framed as PROPOSED and never as a deletion or removal of the non-generating invariants.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 5 -- The liveness question (governance) The system's liveness-freeness is a theorem (TV-F-007.3). Whether KnowledgeOS should carry liveness obligations ... is a design decision -- formulate the question precisely, decide nothing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 5 explicitly separates a proven mathematical fact (the system's liveness-freeness is a theorem, TV-F-007.3) from a distinct, undecided governance/design question -- whether KnowledgeOS should carry liveness obligations (citing '048 section 48.9's example and K7's capability being upgraded to an occurrence obligation as illustrative material) -- with the instruction to formulate the question precisely but decide nothing under this plan.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PASS criteria: Step 1-2 complete when every statement has exactly one KI row and one layer; Step 3 per-layer PASS = explicit model; FAIL = minimal unsatisfiable subset exhibited; OPEN = named missing interpretation. Circularity check ... runs alongside Step 3.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines PASS criteria: Steps 1-2 are complete only when every invariant statement has exactly one KI row and exactly one layer assignment; per layer in Step 3, PASS requires an explicit model, FAIL requires a minimal unsatisfiable subset to be exhibited, and OPEN requires naming the specific missing interpretation. Requires a circularity check (referencing two previously-flagged circularity findings, a goal/policy recursion and an identity bootstrap circularity) to run alongside Step 3.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Prerequisites (why this stage waits) UL canonical meanings for the COLLIDING terms (plan 01) - fresh-ID invariant catalogue with layers (plan 08 steps 1-2, because the corpus's own boundary-derivation method [162] derives contexts from invariants) - the residence dispositions
a_rows_sample.statement: States why the DDD verification stage must wait on three prerequisites: canonical ubiquitous-language meanings for the terms flagged as COLLIDING in plan 01 (especially Assessment/Assertion); the fresh-ID consolidated invariant catalogue with layer assignments from plan 08 steps 1-2, explicitly because the corpus's own boundary-derivation method (step 162) derives bounded contexts FROM invariants, not the reverse; and prior residence dispositions (evidence and Zero findings), since those are themselves aggregate-boundary decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L. Next attack KI-catalogue consolidation (mechanical, high-value, ungated) + derivation chain D-1 (the 8-primitive constructibility claims -- the corpus's central "everything follows" claim, never yet tested). Both executable without any governance input.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends the single next attack as two ungated, governance-independent tasks: the mechanical KI-catalogue consolidation (plan 08, high value) and derivation chain D-1, testing the 8-primitive constructibility claims -- described as the corpus's central 'everything follows' claim, never yet tested.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Perform the mandatory joint-satisfiability test. Given all surviving invariants: Does there exist at least one state satisfying all of them simultaneously? If not proven, mark: JOINT_SATISFIABILITY = UNVERIFIED. If a counterexample demonstrates inconsistency: JOINT_SATISFIABILITY = REFUTED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a joint-satisfiability test over all surviving invariants -- does at least one state satisfy them all simultaneously -- marked JOINT_SATISFIABILITY = UNVERIFIED absent a proof, or REFUTED if a counterexample demonstrates inconsistency; explicitly forbids accepting an invariant collection merely because each invariant individually looks reasonable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does there exist at least one valid KnowledgeOS state satisfying all mandatory invariants simultaneously? If this has not been established, mark the theory accordingly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the mandatory joint-satisfiability requirement over all mandatory invariants (does at least one valid KnowledgeOS state satisfy them all simultaneously), explicitly forbidding verifying each invariant only independently, and requiring the theory to be marked accordingly if joint satisfiability has not been established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KI-ID ... satisfiability status ... whether it is definitional, epistemic, governance, architectural or empirical ... Does the intended interpretation of the consolidated invariant system have at least one model? ... Do not confuse: there exists a model under arbitrary interpretations with: the intended KnowledgeOS semantics are jointly satisfiable
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a fresh KI-ID invariant catalogue (source, exact statement, semantic meaning, duplicate group, layer, MUST/SHOULD status, assumptions, logical dependencies, satisfiability status, definitional/epistemic/governance/architectural/empirical classification) and draws a sharp distinction between a model existing under arbitrary interpretations versus the intended KnowledgeOS semantics being jointly satisfiable -- these are stated to be different claims not to be confused.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V = { x | I1(x) ∧ I2(x) ∧ ... ∧ In(x) } ... Determine whether: V is non-empty; V is empty; V is unknown; V is non-empty only under additional assumptions. If the invariant system is unsatisfiable, the theory cannot simply be declared valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes joint invariant satisfiability as V={x | I1(x)^...^In(x)} and requires explicitly determining whether V is non-empty, empty, unknown, or non-empty only under stated additional assumptions, with an explicit rule that an unsatisfiable invariant system blocks declaring the theory valid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Joint satisfiability (§11) NOT YET INVESTIGATED ... The question is not open — it is currently ill-posed, and saying so is the honest result
a_rows_sample.statement: States that joint invariant satisfiability (V={x | I1(x)^...^In(x)}) cannot yet be evaluated given only 1 of roughly 500 invariants is decidable, and explicitly reclassifies this from 'open question' to 'currently ill-posed', framing that reclassification itself as the honest result rather than a gap to be filled.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Answer: NO for the formalizable core. The invariant system is INCONSISTENT ... FIVE INDEPENDENT minimal conflicting subsets
a_rows_sample.statement: Answers the standing joint-satisfiability question (can all surviving invariants hold simultaneously) for the formalizable core: NO, the system is inconsistent, decomposing into five independent minimal conflicting subsets, four of which conflict within a single step or between two steps step-100 declares closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A naive reading concludes the satisfiability question is ill-posed. That reading is too weak, and I reject it ... yields a sound lower bound on inconsistency
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the weaker 'ill-posed' framing of joint satisfiability (given only 1 of ~500 invariants is a decidable predicate), arguing satisfiability requires only that commitments be formalizable enough to admit a truth assignment, not that every invariant be individually decidable; the resulting propositional-abstraction method yields a sound lower bound on inconsistency, since it cannot find conflicts hidden inside undefined predicates.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 14 atoms, each with a verbatim source ... atoms: 14 models enumerated: 16,384 SATISFYING MODELS: 0
a_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a 14-atom propositional abstraction of the corpus's own boxed commitments (each atom traced to a verbatim source, e.g. UnknownRepresentable from step-089's I_VerificationState, DiscardPermitted/ProofOfNonNecessity/FutureQuestionsKnowable from steps 088/098, OneOwnerPerConcept and FindingLifecycleSplit from step 138, EpistemicPartialOrder/EpistemicTotalChain from step 192, EntropyNonIncreasing/EntropyGrows from step 188, SemanticElevationGoverned/SemanticDemotionGoverned, FreezeDeletesTerms from 201-A) and exhaustively enumerates all 2^14=16,384 possible truth assignments, finding exactly zero satisfying models.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MCS-1 Unknown semantics ... The corpus's own runtime verification surface cannot express the third value its own invariant mandates ... Three defects in one artifact
a_rows_sample.statement: MCS-1: step-089's I_VerificationState mandates a runtime that supports True/False/Unknown, but step-099's actual runtime dashboard value domain is verified first-hand to be {PASS,DEGRADED,FAIL} with no Unknown -- compounded by the same dashboard also displaying I_Security (a conjunction over four non-existent conjuncts) and a never-minted I_ArchitectureConformance, three defects in one artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MCS-2 Retention ... A1 ∧ A2 ⊢ ¬∃X : Discard(X), contradicting A3 ... A1 and A2 are two sections apart in the same file
a_rows_sample.statement: MCS-2: formalizes the retention conflict as three axioms (A1: discard requires provable universal non-necessity across all protected future questions; A2: future questions are generally unknowable; A3: some discarding is required or storage grows unboundedly) and derives that A1 and A2 together entail no discarding is ever provable, directly contradicting A3 -- with A1 and A2 stated two sections apart in the same file (step 088) and never reconciled, while step-100 declares both step-088 and step-098 closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MCS-3 Aggregate ownership ... The Finding state machine therefore has three owners under a rule demanding exactly one — within one file
a_rows_sample.statement: MCS-3: step-138's own §138.49 boxes 'exactly one authoritative owner' per concept while its own §138.26 distributes the Finding lifecycle across three bounded contexts, giving Finding three owners under a rule demanding exactly one within the same file; cross-references step-149's ownership matrix violating the same rule from a different direction (an 'Action | Action/Agent' disjunctive owner).

b_rows_sample.anchor: grep -oE '^```[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*' over all 17 files returns exactly two fence types: bare ``` and ```text — 62 fences, zero language-tagged
b_rows_sample.statement: Global execution-evidence sweep across all 17 audited files: exactly 62 code fences, all bare/```text, zero language-tagged; zero hits for reproducibility/execution-log keywords; no file contains an executed computation, command output, solver invocation, dataset, or sample size; every one of ~190 'PASS' tokens is an author-written label, not a test result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §26.21 `Sufficient(E,q)` — NOT_DEFINED, oracle ... §26.41 observability matrix ... Kalman rank condition, correctly stated
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-026 (model boundary/observability/identifiability) verdict: definitions PARTIALLY_CLEAR (pi, ~_O, identifiability, observability matrix CLEAR; Sufficient(E,q), InformationLoss, ModelContract, ModelCritique, CanJustify NOT_DEFINED); five uncited re-derivations of earlier steps 013/014/016/020/023 identified; computability stops at DEFINED (INPUTS_KNOWN fails); all seven 'falsification experiments' are AUTHOR_ASSERTED_PASS with no inputs/system/output.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is this axis the same decomposition as step-020's 8 TYPES ... NO — it is a FORK, not a refinement
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-027's U(H) 8-vector (measurement/epistemic/aleatoric/model/semantic/identity/temporal/causal, partitioning uncertainty by causal origin in the pipeline) is an uncited FORK against step-020's 8 TYPES (partitioning the logical/representational shape of an unknown) -- two orthogonal, unreconciled 8-way taxonomies over the same symbol space, plus a third incompatible 5-term U-decomposition (U_D) in the same file 39 sections later.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contradiction(A,B) iff Context(A)≈Context(B) ∧ A⊨¬B — ILL-TYPED ... FIRST INVALID INFERENCE, §28.44
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-028's conflict/contradiction formalism is load-bearing on an undefined context-similarity relation (Context(A)≈Context(B)); its non-explosion/containment invariant is stipulated, not derived; the file's first invalid inference (§28.44) presupposes a well-defined containment boundary that classical logic with a functionality axiom for Version would not actually respect, requiring an unspecified paraconsistent or relevance-logic mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A satisfying assignment does not 'may' exist; it demonstrably DOES exist ... §29.24 ... ASSERTED, NOT ARGUED
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-029's worked SAT example ((A∨B)∧(¬A∨C)) is verifier-recomputed to have 4 satisfying models, contradicting the source's hedge 'may exist'; the file's 'no SMT solver needed everywhere' decision criterion is asserted with no complexity claim, no cost model, and no classification procedure for 'simple' vs solver-requiring constraints, while its own companion meta file lists complexity analysis as 'Not yet analyzed'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Brier ... correct ... log-loss is undefined (−∞ penalty) at p∈{0,1} on a wrong call — no clipping/ε convention is specified ... §30.59 ... fully executable test that was not executed
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-030's Brier score and log-loss formulas are verified mathematically correct, but log-loss is left undefined at p in {0,1} with no epsilon-clipping convention specified (precisely the failure mode a KnowledgeOS asserting P=1.0 would hit); its ten falsification experiments are all AUTHOR_ASSERTED_PASS, and §30.59 is flagged as the single most damaging unexecuted-but-fully-executable test in the 17-file scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M1 — Type correctness ... M7 — Computational feasibility ... step-031, which is explicitly commissioned to be this gate, never once references M1–M7 by name
b_rows_sample.statement: The step-030-analysis meta file's M1-M7 review gate (type/semantic/composability/uncertainty/temporal/contradiction-safety/computational-feasibility correctness) is commissioned as Step 31's task but never applied by step-031, which substitutes a different 12-category A-L classification instead; grep for 'M1' across step-031 returns zero hits -- registered as VC-10.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 31 ... THE LOAD-BEARING FILE ... TWO ILL-TYPINGS IN ONE LINE ... IS THE UPGRADE EARNED BY ANYTHING IN §31.69? NO
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-031 (the corpus's designated formal audit) is found ILL-TYPED at its own type universe (undeclared P, colliding V symbol, untyped sigma, colliding G=(V,E)); its status upgrade to 'Structurally Sound + Mathematically Coherent at the Core' (§31.70) is ruled unearned on four independent grounds (coherence undefined while the proof calculus is OPEN; no new evidence beyond a mostly oracle-gated/circular counterexample set; the upgrade's own §31.75 'no contradiction' line is refuted by two in-file contradictions VC-1/VC-2; and it reverses the commissioning meta-file's calibrated verdict on no new evidence) -- called a relabelling, not a finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CE tally: genuinely derivable ... CE4, CE5, CE13, CE16 (4/20) ... circular ... oracle ... ill-posed ... not actually tested
b_rows_sample.statement: Of step-031's twenty counterexamples CE1-CE20, verifier re-derivation classifies only 4 as genuinely derivable from the file's own §31.1-31.48 definitions (CE4, CE5, CE13, CE16), 4 as circular axiom-restatements, 7 as gated on undefined oracles or silently imported from uncited earlier steps, 1 as ill-posed (vacuous), and 1 (CE11) as not actually tested despite being labelled 'PASS conceptually'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §32.34 ... immediately self-invalidated at §32.34's own next line ... §32.79 ... a fourth competing spine object
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-032's Status(A) six-value enum is declared and then withdrawn as non-mutually-exclusive within the same section; its EpistemicClaim EC 11-tuple is identified as a fourth competing 'spine' object alongside step-031's 6-tuple assertion, 7-tuple K_t, and its own 5-tuple State(A); its Belnap-FOUR-equivalent lattice claim is neither named nor cited as Belnap's bilattice, and no join/meet operation is ever defined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §33.29 Y=X^2 ... This is the single best worked example in the 17-file scope ... §33.76 Risk = Uncertainty × Consequence ... the only place in the scope where a slogan is retracted in favour of its formal counterpart
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-033 (uncertainty propagation) is rated the strongest derivation record in the 17-file scope -- every numeric propagation (delta method, covariance, interval arithmetic including the non-monotone X^2 example, Bayesian model averaging, minimax regret) checks out under verifier re-derivation, and it contains the scope's only self-correction of a slogan ('Risk=Uncertainty x Consequence') back to its formal definition (Risk(a)=E[L(a,Y)]); nonetheless all its interval computations are three-line hand calculations, never executed as code, and Sigma/priors are never populated with data.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §34.5 EVPI=L_0-L_PI ... EVPI≥0 is guaranteed and the file does not state it ... §34.6 Cost(I) ... ill-typed in retrospect
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-034's EVPI/EVSI/NVOI decision-theoretic core is verified correct and re-derives step-015's EVSI with zero citation; several free non-negativity invariants (EVPI>=EVSI>=0) go unstated; its scalar Cost(I) in NVOI=EVSI(I)-Cost(I) becomes ill-typed in retrospect once step-035 §35.39 redefines Cost as a 5-vector without noting the break (VC-5).

b_rows_sample.anchor: §35.24 ... NP-hard in general ... TRUE but UNPROVED ... §35.75's boxed conclusion ... NOT_DERIVED ... FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: §35.75
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-035's portfolio-optimization NP-hardness claim is judged true but unproved (no reduction, no approximation ratio, and its own §35.27 constructs a supermodular case for which the greedy bound explicitly fails); its boxed conclusion that 'the mathematical architecture does not inherently require a supercomputer' is ruled NOT_DERIVED because 3 of the 8 listed operation families (constraint checking/SAT, optimization, Bayesian inference) are precisely the ones already shown intractable two sections earlier.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §36.7 ... verbatim duplicates of step-030 §30.8–30.9, uncited ... The file states the requirement it violates two pages earlier ... §36.49 ... 8-tuple H ... vs §36.80 ... 6-tuple
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-036's calibration/meta-validation layer duplicates step-030's Brier/log-loss formulas uncited, then internally violates its own later-stated requirement (SE and sample size for every meta-metric) with the same undated formulas; it defines two incompatible 'health/meta' vectors (8-tuple H at §36.49 vs 6-tuple MetaState_t at §36.80, VC-7) and boxes a 4-kind drift family that silently omits 4 of the 6 drift kinds it had just enumerated (VC-8).

b_rows_sample.statement: Step-037's adversarial-epistemology layer labels a one-player optimization as 'game-theoretic reasoning' with no opponent strategy space or equilibrium concept defined; it misattributes step-026's identifiability foundation to Step 31 (itself an uncited restatement of step-026); its own adversarial/strategic-actor assumption is never propagated into steps 038-040, which revert to a neutral-source model (VC-9).

b_rows_sample.anchor: §38.17 ... the only place in the scope where a numerical counterexample is actually constructed ... §38.35 ... the only place in 17 files where the aggregate pattern is used correctly and load-bearingly
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-038 (identity/entity resolution) contains the scope's only genuinely constructed numerical counterexample (sim(A,B)=0.95, sim(B,C)=0.95, sim(A,C)=0.60 defeating transitive closure at threshold 0.9) and its only correct load-bearing use of the DDD aggregate pattern (AggregateIdentity), but 'Similarity(x,y)' -- load-bearing for the entire file's argument -- is never defined, and the counterexample's own transitive closure is never actually run.

b_rows_sample.anchor: §39.16 ... the single most mathematically mature sentence in the corpus ... §39.47 ... pigeonhole ... §39.49 correctly refuses to equate semantic information with Shannon entropy
b_rows_sample.statement: Step-039 (bounded-context translation) is rated the strongest DDD file in the scope, correctly using standard DDD vocabulary (Anti-Corruption Layer, context map, per-context Ubiquitous Language) and containing a correctly-hedged information-theoretic argument (deterministic translation cannot increase entropy, but H(A)>H(B) is evidence of possible loss, not proof of semantic invalidity, via a pigeonhole-forced lossy 3-to-2 status mapping example); its core notion 'Meaning(x|C)' is nonetheless never defined anywhere in the 17-file scope despite being load-bearing for every lossless/lossy determination.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step-040 introduces a third, unreconciled contradiction definition (after step-028 and step-031's), a conflict-state enum that silently grows from 5 to 9 members with no migration note, and an Authority(a,c,d) that drops the proposition and time arguments of step-028's Authority(S,H,C,t) -- directly contradicting step-028's own boxed 'Authority is proposition-specific' (VC-3) -- while also containing the scope's only correct stated complexity bound on a concrete operation (O(|V_affected|+|E_affected|) dependency traversal, §40.41).

b_rows_sample.statement: The post-Step-40 review's four-artifact mandate (mathematical definition / DDD interpretation / software abstraction / executable falsification tests, replacing 'Concept->PASS' with 'Mathematics->DDD->Software->Test') is read by the verifier as the corpus's own admission that Steps 26-40 produced exactly Concept->PASS and nothing more; the mandate binds only Step 41 onward and does not retroactively require re-testing steps 26-40.

b_rows_sample.statement: The post-Step-40 review's self-labelled 'architectural judgment estimate' progress bars are found unsupportable at the Implementation (~30%, against zero source files in the corpus) and Verification (~15%, against only author-asserted PASS labels) rows, though the disclaimer distinguishing them from measured metrics is itself judged good practice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus contains TWO separate kernel lineages, each internally coherent and genuinely evolving, which COMPETE with one another and are never reconciled. It is not one evolving theory. EQUIVALENT: 0 pairs, CONSERVATIVE EXTENSION: 7 pairs, COMPETING: 27 pairs, INCOMPARABLE: 2 pairs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed pairwise comparison (by role, not name) of all nine candidate KnowledgeOS kernels answers the Reconciliation Gate's central question: the corpus contains TWO separate, internally-coherent, genuinely-evolving kernel lineages that COMPETE with each other and are never reconciled -- NOT one evolving theory. Of 36 kernel pairs: 0 equivalent, 7 conservative extension, 27 competing, 2 incomparable.

a_rows_sample.statement: Nine candidate kernels are catalogued with exact components and origin: K0/7-frame (pre-070), K_OS 8-tuple (070 SS70.1), K_L 7-tuple (070 SS70.21), amended 8-tuple (073 SS73.63), 201-A freeze 16-term, Step 230 v0 6-tuple (opening), Step 230 v1 5-tuple (SS230.31), Step 232 v2 6-tuple (SS232.41), Step 232 inner mathfrak K 5-tuple (SS232.1) -- Steps 234-236 introduce no new kernel, reusing 232's mathfrak K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BEFORE ... not closed ... REPAIR ... §232.41 adds P ... AFTER -- the nine tests: 1. Closure YES -- repaired. 2. Well-typedness NO. ... 5. Composability NO -- and Step 232 proves it itself. ... 9. Historical continuity NO.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal before/repair/after test of the 230->232 closure repair against the Reconciliation Gate's 9 required properties: only closure is repaired (Policy added, time re-handled as a sequence index); well-typedness, totality, determinism, composability (Step 232 itself proves T1,T2 in T_G but T2 o T1 not in T_G), computability, minimality, independence, and historical continuity ALL remain unresolved -- the repair is REAL but PARTIAL, fixing exactly one of nine properties, vindicating the earlier warning that 'a repair that makes a definition larger is not automatically a successful repair'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I*={Provenance} -- the only invariant in all nine historical phases (PHASE-LEDGER). Provenance appears in only 5 of 9 kernels, and in neither 230 v1 nor 232 v2. ... The one concept present in every phase of the 182-step history is demoted to a derived quantity by the latest kernels.
a_rows_sample.statement: The decisive convergence finding: three independent methods (executed regex over 182 sources finding I*={Provenance}; executed role-comparison finding Provenance in only 5/9 kernels, absent from BOTH current kernels 230v1 and 232v2; and the formal counterexample showing L=History(T) fails to derive external provenance at t=0) converge on the sharpest structural finding of the reconciliation gate: the history's only universal invariant is absent from the kernel claiming to reconstruct that history, and the argument for its absence (L=History(T)) does not itself hold.

a_rows_sample.anchor: transformation 8/9 <- the only near-universal primitive. policy 6/9. ... transformation is the only role appearing in 8 of 9 kernels. If any single primitive is historically warranted, it is that one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed role-coverage count across all nine kernels: transformation appears in 8/9 (the only near-universal primitive), policy 6/9, {event,provenance,artifact,invariant,state,type} 5/9 each, {context,evidence,authority} 4/9, {status,identity,lineage} 2/9, {graph,temporalvalidity,observation,decision,assessment,action} 1/9 -- transformation being the one role historically warranted as a primitive is consistent with the corpus's own headline 'KnowledgeOS approx Governed Knowledge State Transformation System'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 236 (written 10:13:01) reproduces this verification programme's findings and labels them direct evidence. ... Step 236 attributes these to 'one of the audit artifacts' and 'the corpus audit' -- this programme, unnamed.
a_rows_sample.statement: A systemic finding: Step 236 (primary corpus, written 10:13:01) reproduces this verification programme's own prior findings (from an artifact written 09:00:36) nearly verbatim -- the '6 of 182 steps named, 0 quoted, 176 absent' finding, the 'EL=empty set' notation, the 'four-to-five-step deferral chain' phrase -- attributing them anonymously to 'one of the audit artifacts'/'the corpus audit' without naming this verification programme.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I decline to treat Step 236 as independent corroboration of my own findings. ... Step 236 is recorded as a corpus response to this audit, not as evidence for it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Circularity-hazard response: the verifier explicitly declines to treat Step 236 as independent corroboration of its own prior findings, since doing so would merely confirm its own analysis reflected back at itself -- Step 236 is instead recorded as a corpus RESPONSE to this audit, not as evidence FOR it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 236 says: We now have direct evidence. My findings are class D -- reasoned verifier conclusions from textual analysis. They are not direct evidence, and not empirical evidence about any software. §11 forbids exactly this upgrade.
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence-class inflation is found: Step 236 labels the reproduced findings 'direct evidence', but the verifier's own findings are evidence class D (reasoned conclusions from textual analysis) -- not direct evidence and not empirical evidence about any software; the Reconciliation Gate's own SS11 explicitly forbids exactly this kind of evidence-class upgrade.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 213 boxes AI Interpretation\neq Engineering Evidence. This verification programme is AI interpretation. Step 236 treats it as evidence. ... Step 236's conclusion is correct, and responding to an audit is better practice than the corpus's usual uncited re-derivation. ... The defect is the eviden
a_rows_sample.statement: The corpus is found to break its own rule (Step 213's boxed AI-Interpretation != Engineering-Evidence) at the very first opportunity to apply it reflexively, since this verification programme IS AI interpretation and Step 236 treats it as evidence; in fairness, Step 236's underlying conclusion is correct and its act of responding to external audit criticism is credited as a genuine methodological improvement (the first such response in 236 steps) -- the defect identified is specifically the evidence LABEL, not the corrective act itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A -- ESTABLISHED: Nine candidate kernels exist; 27 of 36 pairs compete ... B -- PROVEN UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS ... C -- PLAUSIBLE/PROPOSED: That the two lineages could be unified via artifact->state and invariant->policy. No document proposes this; it is my conjecture. D -- REFUTED/UNDER-SPECIFIE
a_rows_sample.statement: Final 4-class verdict per the gate's own mandated schema: (A) ESTABLISHED -- 9 kernels exist with 27/36 competing pairs, two disjoint never-reconciled lineages, Step 232's two incommensurable structures, the partial closure repair, transformation as the sole near-universal primitive, Provenance as I* yet absent from both current kernels; (B) PROVEN UNDER EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS -- L=History(T) holds for internal lineage only; (C) PLAUSIBLE/PROPOSED -- the two lineages COULD be unified via artifact->state and invariant->policy mappings, explicitly labeled the verifier's own unestablished conjecture, proposed by no corpus document; (D) REFUTED/UNDER-SPECIFIED -- 070's minimality (REFUTED via TV-F-043), 230/232's minimality (UNPROVEN), mathbb K's well-typedness (UNDER-SPECIFIED), kernel independence (REFUTED for both 230 and 232), and 'one evolving theory' itself (REFUTED -- two competing lineages).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I have not chosen a kernel. All nine remain live. ... I have not repaired K's typing, ⊨'s semantics, or the independence failure. Nothing here is empirically validated. Corpus record: 494 files, 238 steps, zero empirical acts.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit discipline statement of what must NOT be concluded from this reconciliation: no kernel has been chosen (all nine remain live), the two lineages have not been merged (the unification conjecture is explicitly the verifier's own, not established), Step 236 has not been treated as corroboration, and nothing here is empirically validated -- corpus record at this point: 494 files, 238 steps, zero empirical acts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O\rightarrow E\rightarrow Q\rightarrow I\rightarrow K and K\rightarrow D\rightarrow A.
b_rows_sample.statement: First correction: a single set K cannot mean 'knowledge' generically -- distinguishes O (Observation), E (Evidence), Q (Claim), I (Inference), K (Accepted Knowledge), D (Decision), A (Action) as different domain objects, giving epistemic progression O->E->Q->I->K and operational progression K->D->A.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C. ... Artifact\neq EpistemicRole. Meaning is contextual.
b_rows_sample.statement: Artifact versus epistemic role: for artifact X, Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C, so Artifact != EpistemicRole -- the same artifact can be evidence in one context and historical knowledge after acceptance in another; 'meaning is contextual' connects DDD directly to the mathematical model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C=(S_C,V_C,R_C,P_C,A_C)
b_rows_sample.statement: Context is formalized beyond a bounded-context name as a 5-tuple C=(S_C semantic vocabulary, V_C validity rules, R_C material distinctions, P_C policies, A_C authority model) -- a DDD bounded context is thus a semantic and governance environment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_1}\neq\llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_2}. Same representation \not\Rightarrow same meaning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Bounded context as semantic space: an object x has meaning through a context-relative denotation [[x]]_C, and the same representation can have different meanings under different contexts ([[x]]_C1 != [[x]]_C2) -- 'same representation does not imply same meaning' is proposed as a mathematical foundation of DDD bounded contexts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x_1\sim_\phi x_2\iff\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2). ... [x]_\phi.
b_rows_sample.statement: Context mapping phi_AB: S_A -> S_B between bounded contexts is not assumed bijective (often partial/many-to-one/one-to-many/conditional/lossy); it induces an equivalence relation x1 ~phi x2 iff phi(x1)=phi(x2) with equivalence classes [x]_phi, giving a rigorous formal handle on information/semantic collapse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticViolation\iff MaterialDistinction\land UncontrolledCollapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Semantic loss is formalized precisely: a collapse phi_AB(x1)=phi_AB(x2) where x1 is not~_A x2 is a candidate semantic-loss event, but is an error (SemanticViolation) only if the collapsed distinction belongs to R_A or R_B (i.e. is material) -- SemanticViolation iff MaterialDistinction and UncontrolledCollapse, much stronger than simply 'preserve semantics'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M_A(x_1,x_2)\land\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2)\Rightarrow DeclaredLoss
b_rows_sample.statement: Context-specific materiality predicate M_C(x1,x2) ('the distinction between x1 and x2 is material in context C') yields the architectural invariant candidate: M_A(x1,x2) and phi(x1)=phi(x2) implies DeclaredLoss for a transformation crossing from A to B.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T=(K_A,C_A,A_t,P_t,E_t,\tau)\rightarrow(K_B,C_B).
b_rows_sample.statement: Transformation T is progressively enriched from a bare (K_A,C_A)->(K_B,C_B) mapping to a full domain operation T=(K_A,C_A,Actor_t,Policy_t,Evidence_t,tau)->(K_B,C_B), with the DDD distinction Command (expresses intent) -> Transformation (domain operation/process) -> Event (records what happened).

b_rows_sample.anchor: L(K_t)=\{(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,\tau_i,C_i)\}. ... KnowledgeOS lineage = typed provenance graph.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lineage is formalized as a typed provenance graph G_L=(V_L,E_L) (nodes=knowledge states/artifacts, edges=transformations carrying metadata (T,A,E,C,tau)), generally a DAG allowing branching (K1->{K2^A,K2^B}) and merging -- substantially stronger than an ordinary version chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Auth(a,r,c,p) mean actor a is authorized under role r, context c, and policy p. ... Identity\neq Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Authority is formalized as a relation Auth(a,r,c,p) (actor, role, context, policy) rather than A=User; an action is legitimate only if Auth(a,r,c,p)=True, giving Identity != Authority (authenticated but not authorized is possible).

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance). ... E_q\xrightarrow{\mathcal I}Q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence is formalized as a 6-tuple E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance) rather than a boolean Evidence=True, supporting a claim Q via an inferential procedure E_q -I-> Q.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \hat F_n\neq F. Observation\neq PopulationTruth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistical interpretation of evidence: the empirical distribution hat F_n(x) estimates but is not identical to the underlying distribution F, giving Observation != PopulationTruth; likewise a confidence interval must never be silently converted into a ProbabilityOfTruth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(\theta\mid E)=\frac{P(E\mid\theta)P(\theta)}{P(E)}. ... Bayesian machinery is one possible formalism for representing uncertainty where the domain permits probabilistic interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Bayesian evidence via Bayes' rule is offered as one possible uncertainty formalism, not a mandatory commitment -- must not be introduced merely because 'KnowledgeOS is probabilistic'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance=DeterministicAssurance\cup StatisticalEvidence\cup HumanJudgement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two assurance modes are distinguished and must not be conflated: Deterministic (I(x)=True/False, e.g. SchemaValid(x)) and Statistical (P(H|E) or an estimator with uncertainty), together with human judgment forming Assurance = DeterministicAssurance union StatisticalEvidence union HumanJudgement; the appropriate mode depends on the invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hash(x)=h. ... P(X>x). ... Meaning(x,C). ... Authorized(a,p). These require different mathematical structures.
b_rows_sample.statement: Architectural properties are classified by kind, each needing different mathematics: exact (Hash(x)=h), empirical (P(X>x)), interpretive (Meaning(x,C)), normative (Authorized(a,p)) -- resolving the previous risk of treating every architectural property as probabilistically quantifiable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Set/Logic + Probability/Statistics + Semantics + Graph Theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS is proposed to span four mathematical domains: Logic (handles invariants), Statistics (uncertainty and empirical evidence), Semantics (meaning and context), Graph theory (lineage and transformation history) -- a more defensible architecture than reducing everything to one equation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord. Each aggregate protects its own invariants.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate DDD aggregate boundaries (avoiding one enormous transactional aggregate): KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord, each with its own invariant -- e.g. KnowledgeItem 'cannot change materially without a recorded transition'; Transformation 'cannot be considered governed without an applicable authority/policy decision'; EvidenceRecord 'cannot silently change after being used to support a claim' (a source change must produce a new evidence state); Decision = f(Evidence,Authority,Context,Policy), not authoritative merely by existing; Policy determines AllowedTransformations/RequiredEvidence/RequiredAuthority/RequiredValidation, giving Policy->GovernedTransformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationRecorded, EvidenceRegistered, ClaimProposed, KnowledgeAccepted, TransformationRequested, TransformationExecuted, ValidationCompleted, DecisionApproved, KnowledgeSuperseded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine candidate domain events forming the temporal history, supporting an event-sourced interpretation K_t = Fold(E_1,...,E_t), i.e. CurrentState = f(EventHistory) -- explicitly noted as an implementation choice, not a mandatory architecture requirement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K=(State,Context,Transformation,Evidence,Authority) with Lineage being generated by the sequence of transformations: L=History(T).
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel is reduced from the original 6-tuple (K,C,T,A,E,L) to a 5-tuple (K,C,T,E,A) by recognizing Lineage L is not independent but generated by the transformation history: L = History(T) -- an important reduction toward the minimal kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SI=f(K,C,T) ... BP=f(C,T) ... EI=f(K,E) ... GA=f(A,T) ... TL=f(T_{1:n}) ... DA=f(E,T,Policy). ... the seven principles may not be seven fundamental architectural primitives. They may be derived properties.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate dependency equations deriving the 6 (of the earlier 7-8) named architectural principles as functions of the minimal kernel: SemanticIntegrity=f(K,C,T), BoundaryPreservation=f(C,T), EpistemicIntegrity=f(K,E), GovernedAction=f(A,T), TemporalLineage=f(T_{1:n}), Assurance/DeterministicAssurance=f(E,T,Policy) -- proposing that these principles may be derived properties rather than independent primitives, precisely the compression the historical audit sought.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 9 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's binding authorization boundary: it is explicitly research-only, not authorized to canonize a kernel, and no result may be promoted to invariant/theorem/ADR/standard by the document itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What this experiment is NOT: a naming exercise ... a retrofit of the current architecture: Part XXIV "existing class != domain primitive" — no architectural circularity ... a canonization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates six things the experiment explicitly is not (naming exercise, aesthetic minimization, a vote, a universal-necessity proof, an architectural retrofit/circularity, or a canonization), each tied to a concrete safeguard already built into the executed model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Those disagreements are results, not defects.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports, as an executed finding, that the three distinct necessity notions (empirically necessary, formally necessary via the reach algebra, and DDD-necessary as a distinct domain responsibility) disagree for the operators Select, Discriminate, and Revise, explicitly framing the disagreement itself as a valid experimental result rather than a flaw in the model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment targets B + C. A result that improves A while worsening B/C is reported as a worse result, per the protocol's final principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms semantic minimality (B) and compositional minimality (C) as the experiment's primary targets, with cardinality (A) explicitly subordinate: an improvement in operator count that worsens semantic or compositional minimality is scored as a worse result overall.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Modification M-1 — C25 added [CORPUS]. ... Without C25, C10 is unrealizable in any model where a Verdict requires evidence ... This modification enlarges the required capability set and therefore makes minimization harder, not easier.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a new capability C25 ('admit an observation as evidence under a policy') to the protocol's original 24-item list, justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) combined with prior constraint 9 (information != evidence) means no capability in C1-C24 covers the observation-to-evidence transition, making C10 (validate) unrealizable without it -- explicitly noted as making minimization harder, not more convenient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C18 reclassified as NON-DISCRIMINATING [NEG]. ... no operator set can fail C18 in this simulator. ... This is a limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies capability C18 (preserve provenance) as non-discriminating because the reach engine structurally guarantees provenance via its derivation DAG for every artifact regardless of operator set, making it untestable by leave-one-out -- explicitly reported as a limitation of the measuring instrument, not a substantive finding about the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C20 given an explicit failure mode: the system must be able to hold >=2 hypotheses and return an UNDECIDED discrimination. It can then fail by overreach — producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives it is determining between.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the under-specified capability C20 (support non-identifiability) with a concrete, falsifiable failure mode (overreach: producing a Determination without being able to represent >=2 held alternatives with an UNDECIDED verdict), preventing the capability from being trivially 'supported' by doing nothing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: merge C2 and C3 (meaning + representation) | corpus explicitly separates Observation != Proposition != Knowledge; merging is tested instead as robustness variant V1 ... merge C12 and C13 (determine + select) | different carriers, different inputs (Inquiry vs Objective); tested as V5
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports two considered-and-rejected capability-model modifications (merging meaning-construction with representation; merging determination with action-selection), each rejected on corpus-grounded or type-grounded reasons but retained as explicit robustness variants (V1, V5) to be tested rather than silently discarded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms ... 'redefine Y so that Y also does X' is mechanically detectable — it is a change to Y's atom set, i.e. a change to the model, not a composition within it -> SMUGGLING = TRUE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the anti-circularity device at the heart of the executed experiment: an operator is identified purely by its declared set of semantic atoms, consulted by the reach engine to the exclusion of operator names, so that redefining one operator to secretly absorb another's function becomes a detectable change to the atom-set model itself (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a legitimate composition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Atoms are deliberately allowed to be shared. A 1:1 operator->atom assignment would make every operator irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous. Two atoms are shared ... and that sharing is where all the interesting results live.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains why two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared between operators rather than assigning each operator a unique atom: a strict 1:1 mapping would make every operator trivially irreducible by construction, rendering the whole ablation experiment vacuous -- the shared atoms are identified as the source of the experiment's most interesting results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Structural concerns (context, time, uncertainty, assumption, provenance, alternatives) are modelled as invariants checked over the reach closure ... not as ownable powers. Making them ownable would have handed one operator a monopoly on, e.g., provenance, and rigged the result.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that structural concerns (context/time/uncertainty/assumptions/provenance/alternatives) are deliberately modelled as invariants checked over the whole reach closure rather than as atoms any single operator could own, to avoid rigging the ablation result by handing one operator an artificial monopoly on a cross-cutting concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: difference-decision ∈ {Discriminate, DetectGap}; norm-comparison ∈ {DetectGap, Determine}. DetectGap holds no atom exclusively. ... it is the assumption most responsible for the headline result, and it is therefore attacked directly by robustness variant V4.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies DetectGap as the only operator in C0-union-Qualify holding no atom exclusively (both its atoms, difference-decision and norm-comparison, are shared with Discriminate and Determine respectively), flagging this modelling choice as the single assumption most responsible for the experiment's headline redundancy result, and explicitly scheduling it for direct attack under robustness variant V4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observe | world-contact | the sole channel for empirical content; nothing downstream may create it | STRONG ... Represent | symbolic-encoding | make semantic content manipulable without asserting it | WEAK ... Qualify | evidential-qualification | admit an observation as evidence under a policy | STR
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the full per-operator contract table (13 C0 operators plus Qualify), each with its claimed atom(s), non-reducible responsibility, and a corpus-support grade from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Relate, Select).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discriminate and DetectGap are all-zero rows. Neither is required by any capability under leave-one-out, because each covers the other's shared atoms. That is not evidence that the capabilities are unneeded — it is evidence that the operator packaging is redundant.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's headline finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are both all-zero rows in the leave-one-out operator-capability matrix, since each can cover the other's shared atoms when the other is removed -- explicitly interpreted not as evidence the underlying capabilities are unneeded but as evidence that the CURRENT OPERATOR PACKAGING of those capabilities is redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C5 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} both removed | the atom difference-decision. C8 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} or {DetectGap, Determine} removed | difference-decision + norm-comparison. A leave-one-out matrix alone would have declared C5 and C8 unnecessary. They are not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that capabilities C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero columns under leave-one-out and become irreducible only under pairwise ablation (C5 lost only when both Discriminate and DetectGap are removed together; C8 lost when either {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are removed together), concretely demonstrating that a leave-one-out-only analysis would have wrongly certified both capabilities as unnecessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A carrier kind is not stamped by the operator that produced it. It is derived from (multiset of input kinds, atoms introduced by this step) -> kind ... Otherwise 'only DetectGap can make a Gap' would be true by fiat and the ablation rigged.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a second anti-circularity device: a derived carrier's kind is determined purely by its input-kind multiset and the atoms introduced, never by which operator produced it, so that any operator set capable of introducing the required atoms over the required inputs can produce a given carrier -- preventing the ablation from being rigged by fiat operator-carrier ownership.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim is producible only via entailment — so its warrant kind is DEDUCTIVE by construction. A Verdict produced by generate-and-test is not a Claim. This is what keeps Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize an honest question rather than a definitional trick.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes, from the carrier-derivation table's type rules, that a Claim can only be produced via the entailment atom (making its warrant kind deductive by construction) while a Verdict produced by generate-and-test (Hypothesize then Validate) is a structurally different carrier -- keeping the composition question 'is Infer equivalent to Validate composed with Hypothesize' a genuinely open, honest question rather than one settled by definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict requires Evidence. This is where the absence of Qualify from C0 becomes fatal. ... Determination requires both NormDelta (hence IdealState) and Inquiry — encoding prior constraint 5, that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives from the type system that a Verdict carrier requires an Evidence input, making the corpus's unimplemented Qualify operator (excluded from C0) fatal to realizing validation without it; separately derives that a Determination carrier requires both a NormDelta (itself requiring IdealState) and an Inquiry, formally encoding the prior constraint that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative directly into the type system rather than merely asserting it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reach(S) = mu A . AMBIENT union {k | exists o in S : k in derive(A, o.atoms)}. Monotone, terminating (finite carrier set), and independent of operator names.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Reach(S) as the least fixpoint (over a finite carrier set, hence terminating and monotone) of applying available operators' atoms to the ambient carriers, with a capability achieved iff its required carrier kinds and atoms are both covered by Reach(S) and the atom pool of S -- the operational definition of formal necessity used throughout the experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No helper functions. ... No helper performs the work of a removed operator — a claim that is mechanically checkable, since helpers cannot introduce atoms.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the reach engine's implementation contains only domain-operator applications plus generic data-structure operations (set union, fixpoint computation), with every helper function classified per the protocol's requirement, and that no helper can perform the work of a removed operator because helpers structurally cannot introduce atoms -- making the no-semantic-smuggling guarantee mechanically checkable rather than merely asserted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Attitude_t = F(Total Evidence_t, Epistemic Standards). ... K_t = F(E_t,S_t). ... S^epi = Epistemic Response Standard / Epistemic Interpretation Policy. This must not be confused with Governance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central derivation: Titelbaum's hypothetical-prior formalism (cr_i=Pr^H(.|E_i)) shows an agent's epistemic attitude is a function of Total Evidence AND Epistemic Standards, not evidence alone, giving K_t=F(E_t,S_t); proposes S^epi (Epistemic Response Standard/Interpretation Policy) as a new KnowledgeOS candidate element explicitly distinct from Governance (Governance = what is permitted/required; S^epi = how evidence is interpreted/weighed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: two agents possess the same total evidence but arrive at different credences because they have different epistemic standards. ... E_t^A=E_t^B does not imply K_t^A=K_t^B.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Titelbaum's same-evidence-different-standards cases to establish that identical total evidence does not entail identical epistemic states, proposing to split the candidate Interpret kernel operator into Interpret(E,S)->M and Update(M,E,S)->K_{t+1} for testing in the kernel-reduction experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = (Content, Source, Acquisition, Context, Time, Provenance). ... AcquisitionModel(e). ... how evidence was obtained can itself be epistemically relevant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the evidence tuple with acquisition context, motivated by Titelbaum's observation-selection-effect discussion (the fish-net sampling example, where knowing short fish could escape through net holes changes how the sample should be interpreted); proposes candidate relations SelectionBias(e,H)/AcquisitionModel(e) belonging to the Evidence/Observation context model rather than the kernel itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A credence value is an attribute of an attitude, not part of the proposition's content. ... k_i=(c_i,kappa_i) ... c_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t) ... kappa_i=(E_i,S_i,Cr_i,Status_i,Provenance_i,Context_i,...)
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Titelbaum's credence-is-an-attitude-not-content distinction to re-split the atomic knowledge-claim tuple into a semantic layer c_i (object, dimension, value, time) and a separate epistemic layer kappa_i (evidence, standards, credence, status, provenance, context), yielding k_i=(c_i,kappa_i) and KnowledgeContent != Confidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: numerical credence can introduce more precision than is actually present. ... EpistemicAttitude = Categorical | Comparative | Ranged | Quantitative | Unknown | Suspended.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against making a single numerical probability the universal epistemic representation, citing Titelbaum's classificatory/comparative/quantitative attitude distinctions, and proposes a non-numeric-friendly EpistemicAttitude type together with an epistemic-resolution concept Resolution(K) rather than assuming all knowledge is exactly quantified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ProbabilityCoherence != Truth != Knowledge. ... Validity = SemanticValidity AND EvidenceAdequacy AND InferentialCoherence AND Calibration AND PurposeAdequacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that Titelbaum's five core Bayesian rules (Non-Negativity, Normality, Finite Additivity, Ratio Formula, Conditionalization) are norms on credences, not truth-establishing rules, yielding ProbabilityCoherence != Truth != Knowledge and proposing CoherenceValidation as only one of five independent validity dimensions (semantic validity, evidence adequacy, inferential coherence, calibration, purpose adequacy).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cr_{t+1}(H)=Cr_t(H|E) ... strict Conditionalization is not sufficient for KnowledgeOS ... Update(K_t,E,mode) -> K_{t+1} ... EvidenceAccumulation != KnowledgeMonotonicity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Conditionalization as a genuine mathematical state-transition model for K_t->K_{t+1}, but notes strict Conditionalization over-commits (learned evidence becomes permanently certain) and cites Jeffrey Conditionalization as the corrective, generalizing to Update(K_t,E,mode)->K_{t+1} that distinguishes hard/soft evidence, partial observation, revised interpretation, changed context, and conflicting evidence -- reinforcing EvidenceAccumulation != KnowledgeMonotonicity (F_t subset-of F_{t+1} coexisting with K_{t+1} revising/retracting prior conclusions).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rel(E,H|C) ... SUPPORTS / REFUTES / IRRELEVANT / CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTS / CONDITIONALLY_REFUTES / SCREENS_OFF / INDEPENDENT ... KnowledgeSpace != {claims}. Instead: KS_t=(K_t,R_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a typed relevance relation Rel(E,H|C) with seven relation types drawn from Titelbaum's independence/positive-relevance/negative-relevance/conditional-relevance/screening-off apparatus, proposed as Knowledge-Space relation types (not kernel primitives), independently converging -- on a formal probabilistic basis -- with an earlier Davidson-derived proposal that Knowledge Space is relational (KS_t=(K_t,R_t)) rather than a bag of claims.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,I_Q) as a condition concerning whether the current epistemic state sufficiently distinguishes the alternatives relevant to inquiry Q. ... This is not Titelbaum's definition of Zero. It is a KnowledgeOS derivation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Titelbaum's doxastically-possible-worlds apparatus to propose Zero as 'failure to eliminate all inquiry-relevant unresolved alternatives' (illustrated by two viable connectivity hypotheses left undistinguished by current evidence), explicitly flagged as a KnowledgeOS-side derivation rather than Titelbaum's own concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicZero != ProbabilisticZero != LogicalFalsehood. ... We should keep Zero semantic rather than identifying it with numerical probability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Titelbaum's Regularity discussion (contingent propositions should not receive credence zero, yet Conditionalization can generate zero credences for evidence-inconsistent propositions) to argue Zero, as a KnowledgeOS gap/defect concept, must remain semantic and not be identified with numerical probability zero or logical falsehood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (K_t,S) where S represents epistemic standards. ... The Hypothetical Priors Theorem establishes that ... a common hypothetical prior [can represent a finite sequence of credence distributions]. ... K_t, S_t, and Governance constraints G are three different things.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts a standard-vs-state distinction: alongside K_t, a stable epistemic-response-standard S (potentially equal to the hypothetical prior Pr^H, which can remain fixed while evidence changes, backed by a cited Hypothetical Priors Theorem) and governance constraints G are three genuinely separate things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: permissive cases where agents with identical evidence can rationally arrive at different credences. ... Adequate(K_1,Q) and Adequate(K_2,Q) may both hold. ... Titelbaum provides independent theoretical support for Adequacy != Uniqueness.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Titelbaum's Objective-vs-Subjective-Bayesianism distinction (subjective Bayesianism permits multiple rationally acceptable credences for identical evidence) as independent theoretical support, alongside an earlier Davidson-derived result, for Adequacy != Uniqueness -- two different states can both be adequate for the same inquiry given different but equally rational epistemic standards.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence -> Relevance -> Confirmation does not automatically yield Confirmation -> Determination. Support != Determination. High Credence != Knowledge. ... Determine(K_t,Q,EC) iff Adequate(K_t,I_Q).
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates confirmation from determination (evidential relevance producing confirmation does not automatically license determination; Support!=Determination; HighCredence!=Knowledge), and proposes replacing a context-free Determine(K_t) kernel operator with an inquiry-relative Determine(K_t,Q,EC) meaning 'determine whether K_t is sufficient to resolve inquiry Q under epistemic constraints EC', equivalent to Adequate(K_t,I_Q).

b_rows_sample.anchor: |E| != EpistemicStrength(E) and EvidenceCount != EvidenceValue. ... E -> Relevance(E,H) -> Confirmation(E,H) -> CredenceChange(H) -> InquiryAdequacy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses Titelbaum's independence/conditional-independence apparatus to state an anti-double-counting principle (evidence item count is not the same as epistemic strength, since correlated or redundant items can masquerade as independent sources), and inserts a relevance-before-value chain refining the earlier expected-information-gain investigation objective to depend on Relevance(E,Q) rather than raw information quantity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: higher-order credences -- credences about one's own credences ... MetaK_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: Raises higher-order epistemic state (MetaK_t, credences about one's own credences) as a further candidate missing KnowledgeOS element, tied to Titelbaum's discussion of an agent's limited access to its own mental state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RespondToEvidence ... Maintain/ApplyEpistemicStandards ... Epistemic Standards may be essential to the KnowledgeOS system without being a kernel operator. ... essential system component vs primitive kernel operation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the kernel-reduction experiment's test list to include whether RespondToEvidence and Maintain/ApplyEpistemicStandards decompose into existing candidate operators (Interpret+Discriminate+Evaluate+Update) or require distinct primitives, explicitly anticipating the possible finding that Epistemic Standards could be an essential SYSTEM component without being a primitive KERNEL operator -- named exactly the kind of distinction the research needs.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence != Epistemic Standards != Attitude != Representation != Confidence != Knowledge != Decision. ... (E_t,S_t) -> K_t -> (E_{t+1},S_{t+1}) -> K_{t+1}. ... Claim_t in K_t but Claim_t not-in K_{t+1} can be legitimate.
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes with a seven-way non-collapse chain (Evidence != Epistemic Standards != Attitude != Representation != Confidence != Knowledge != Decision) and the temporal transformation form K_{t+1}=U(K_t,E_{t+1},S_t^epi,C_{t+1},Q_{t+1}), explicitly allowing a claim present in K_t to be legitimately absent from K_{t+1} when new evidence defeats or revises it -- named the book's deepest contribution over merely 'adding Bayesian probability.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: the single most important missing element exposed by Titelbaum is Epistemic Standards. ... That is a genuine theoretical gap, not merely an architectural enhancement.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the file's bottom-line conclusion: Epistemic Standards is the single most important theoretical gap this reading exposes in KnowledgeOS -- the existing model has evidence, interpretation, inference, validation, K_t, Zero, inquiry and governance, but no explicit place for the mechanism determining how the same evidence gets epistemically evaluated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$(E_t,S_t^{epi})\rightarrow A_t\rightarrow K_t$$ ... \(S_t^{epi}\) = epistemic response standards ... This is **not Governance**. Governance determines what a system is authorized or required to do. Epistemic standards determine how evidence is evaluated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates and sharpens the core S^epi (Epistemic Response Standard) proposal: the compressed chain E_t -> K_t is replaced by (E_t, S_t^epi) -> A_t -> K_t, with S^epi explicitly distinguished from Governance (Governance = what is authorized/required; S^epi = how evidence is evaluated).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Model A -- standard as state K_t=(E_t,S_t^{epi},A_t,...) ... Model B -- standard as configuration ... Model C -- standard as learned state ... Model D -- standards emerge from kernel operations ... Titelbaum actually distinguishes **ongoing** standards from **ultimate** standards
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes four unresolved candidate models for the ontological status of the epistemic-standard object S^epi: (A) standard as part of the state K_t, (B) standard as external configuration outside K_t, (C) standard as a learned state updated via U_S(S_t,E_t), (D) standards emergent from kernel operations F(history,validation,experience); explicitly left undecided, motivated by Titelbaum's own ongoing-vs-ultimate-standards distinction.
