a_rows_sample.anchor: Coextension without Identity -- Ruling: YES -- constitutional, and KnowledgeOS could NOT exist without it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Special Area C ruling: Similarity != Identity is the identity law's limit case; removing it lets extension->identity at any degree of match, up to perfect coextension, collapsing KnowledgeOS into exactly the similarity engine it refuses to be; 'there is no degree of observable match at which the corruption is absent' (a decisive failure test). Consequence: one of the strongest KERNEL rows -- its deep form (Representation != Identity) carried by law 1; the typed encoding is representation, deferred.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Result: only TWO of the five are fundamental architectural absences -- persistent epistemic identity and historical belief evolution
a_rows_sample.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly). Conclusion: the constitutional justification rests on exactly the two fundamental absences (mapping to laws 1 and 11), not a general 'LLMs are bad at X' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopted Constitutional Core -- the smallest possible set (11 laws)
a_rows_sample.statement: The 11-law Adopted Constitutional Core (P5's validated recommendation, NOT adopted law here): 1 Identity Law; 2 Dimension Law; 3 Authority Law; 4 Decision Law; 5 Projection Law; 6 Verification Law; 7 Failure-state Law; 8 Contradiction Law; 9 Unknown Law; 10 Agency Law; 11 History Law -- each independently failure-tested (removing it opens a distinct, named corruption not covered by any other law's removal-test); the 4 Established rows appear unchanged as the spine of laws 3-5; the 22 surviving candidate rows render into the 11 laws without loss of content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Selected kernel law (final wording) ... Failure signature (if removed)
a_rows_sample.statement: The 11 laws given final selected wording with their rendered rows and failure signatures, reproduced from the P5 Decision Matrix (Identity Law renders INV-KOS-002+Context-001+Context-002+Relationship-001+Relation-001; Dimension Law renders INV-KOS-001+NonInterference-001 with NonInterference merged per Decision 2a; Authority Law renders INV-001+INV-003+Pramana-001; Decision Law renders INV-002+Decision-001; Projection Law renders INV-004; Verification Law renders Inference-001+Justification-001+Reasoning-Separation-001+Reasoning-Provenance-001+Vyapti-001+EvidenceAuthenticity-001+Pramana-001; Failure-State Law renders Fallacy-001(state)+Failure-001; Contradiction Law renders Contradiction-001+Dialogue-001(boundary); Unknown Law renders H-ZERO-001+Uncertainty-001+Abhava(requirement); Agency Law renders Agent-001+Relationship-001(knower-side); History Law renders Revisability-001+Temporal family). Verdict: ACCEPTED -- all eleven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context-001 -> Context-002 (law 1's context clause): Context is part of identity: a knowledge object carries its delimiting conditions (its semantic frame) and is never valid beyond them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision 2b: H-KOS-Context-001 (semantic frame preservation) and H-KOS-Context-002 (Avacchedaka, delimiting conditions) are ruled to be the same constitutional content -- 'meaning requires its boundary' -- and render as one clause of the Identity Law with final frozen wording. Rows rendered: H-KOS-Context-001, H-KOS-Context-002; the delimiting-conditions tuple (Entity.Property.Context.Relation.Time.Authority) remains a deferred REPRESENTATION technique -- the principle is the law, the tuple is one way to express it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 1 -- Identity: 1. ... preserve the identity of knowledge ... 3. Similarity SHALL NOT become identity ... 4. Context SHALL remain part of identity ... 5. Knowledge SHALL be a relationship
a_rows_sample.statement: Article 1 (Identity), 5 SHALL/SHALL-NOT clauses: preserve identity across representation/expression/projection changes; representation/expression SHALL NOT become meaning; similarity SHALL NOT become identity (including perfect coextension); context SHALL remain part of identity (delimiting conditions/semantic frame; a claim without its frame is incomplete); knowledge SHALL be a relationship (knower.process.object), never a detached object. Renders INV-KOS-002, H-KOS-Context-001, H-KOS-Context-002, H-KOS-Relationship-001, H-KOS-Relation-001. Failure if removed: Document=Knowledge, vector match=identity, context-free claims, detached free-floating truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ziran suggests that identity is transformational and contextual (not fixed and intrinsic). ... this challenges the Kernel's identity invariant in three fundamental ways.
a_rows_sample.statement: Core challenge: the Kernel identity invariant assumes identity is fixed (immutable Value Object), intrinsic (property of the entity), and assigned/forced (mechanism-imposed); Daoist ziran ('self-so', opposite of wei/forcing) suggests identity is instead transformational, contextual, and natural, drawn from Daodejing ch.25/37/51 and Zhuangzi ch.2/13 plus Ames & Hall, Moeller, and Ziporyn scholarly interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fixed Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (immutable UUID) ... Transformational Identity: Knowledge entity has identity that transforms with knowledge (e.g., K123-UNKNOWN -> K123-VALIDATED -> K123-SUPERSEDED). ... Test: Can the Kernel support transformational identity (not just fixed identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Fixed-vs-transformational identity challenge with worked example and a falsification test asking whether the Kernel can support identity that transforms across the epistemic lifecycle (UNKNOWN->VALIDATED->SUPERSEDED) rather than remaining a static immutable UUID.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Intrinsic Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (intrinsic property). Identity is the same in all contexts. ... Contextual Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123-in-Context-C1 ... Can the Kernel support contextual identity (not just intrinsic identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Intrinsic-vs-contextual identity challenge with worked example and falsification test, drawing on Daodejing ch.2's paired-opposites passage and Zhuangzi ch.2's 'no intrinsic identity' claim to ask whether identity should be relational to context rather than a bare intrinsic property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Forced Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (assigned by mechanism). ... Natural Identity: Knowledge entity has identity that arises naturally from the knowledge itself (e.g., hash of knowledge content, not assigned by mechanism). ... Can the Kernel support natural identity (not just forced identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Forced-vs-natural identity challenge with worked example (a content-derived hash versus a mechanism-assigned identifier) and falsification test, grounded in Daodejing ch.37's 'the myriad things would transform of themselves (ziran)' and Zhuangzi ch.2's 'the sage does not force things to be what they are not.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ziran does not say the Kernel's identity invariant is wrong. Instead, ziran challenges the Kernel to explicitly investigate whether its identity invariant is complete ... Ziran suggests the Kernel should support transformational identity (not necessarily replace fixed identity).
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit discipline: a philosophical observation (ziran challenges completeness) is kept separate from an architectural decision (what the Kernel should do); ziran is read as calling for the Kernel to potentially support (add), not necessarily replace, transformational/contextual/natural identity alongside fixed/intrinsic/forced identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Strong Historical Evidence ... Strong Scholarly Interpretation ... Philosophical Inference ... Architectural Speculation ... Unknown: Whether the Kernel should support transformational, contextual, and natural identity (architectural decision, not philosophical observation).
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence Boundary table graded into five tiers (Strong Historical Evidence, Strong Scholarly Interpretation, Philosophical Inference, Architectural Speculation, Unknown), explicitly leaving the final architectural question in the Unknown tier and closing with an explicit self-restraint: 'DO NOT DESIGN THE KERNEL. DO NOT CHANGE ITS BOUNDARY. DO NOT INTRODUCE NEW DOMAIN CONCEPTS. CHALLENGE THE ARCHITECTURE; DO NOT BECOME ITS ARCHITECT.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: six-way separation: identity != role != eligibility != authorization != ownership != continuation.
a_rows_sample.statement: The design principle of the AST-017 session-bootstrap resolver: six distinct concepts kept as separate first-class report blocks so that none silently substitutes for another (e.g. identity never reaches a gate as a grant).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AST-017 delegates ALL workflow interpretation to AST-015 (fold/identity/authorized) with exactly one bounded raw-record read (the V-3 handoff fact); provider-independent by construction (no model call).
a_rows_sample.statement: States the resolver's core structural guarantee later independently falsification-tested in S0315: a single narrowly-bounded exception to full delegation, and no dependency on which LLM provider is running the session.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the divergence is NOT model-dependent. Two AI providers working the same repository, same workflow records, same injected context resolve the same governed session differently -- and both cannot. The defect is coordination legibility, not model capability.
a_rows_sample.statement: The measured finding motivating the entire session-bootstrap correction saga: session-resolve.php returned AMBIGUOUS with 4 candidates for a session that genuinely held its lane, because process identity lived only in free-text executionContext with no queryable handoff-fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the recorded refusals ('I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable') were correct under the rules. The tooling gave those sessions no lawful way to proceed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes a correctly-fail-closed behavior from a missing lawful exit, framing the fix as adding a route rather than relaxing the safety rule that produced the refusal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: poison-test methodology: inject decoy fields (fake mutationOwner, workItemState, sessions dict, top-level authorizationLinkage, a decoy 'handoffs' array outside transitions) into a valid workflow record and verify the resolver reports only from the documented derived fields, ignoring every decoy.
a_rows_sample.statement: A falsification methodology (labelled F1-F14 plus L1-L3 live-record probes) for verifying that a resolver reads exactly its documented inputs and no more; found the resolver's handoff read is a strict subset of the underlying fold's handoffsTo, so it can only ever over-report 'not ready', never under-report.

a_rows_sample.anchor: recorded_human_start_act is inferred as state != 'CREATED', but a lane CANCELLED directly from CREATED (no START ever recorded) reports recorded_human_start_act=true -- a false statement about the record (finding V-1).
a_rows_sample.statement: A concrete falsifying probe (REGISTER S-c then CANCEL S-c with no START) showing an entailment that holds only in the forward direction (CREATED implies no-START) being relied on in the reverse (not-CREATED implies START-recorded), producing a factually false report field though the system still fails safe (authorized_to_act still requires ACTIVE state).

a_rows_sample.anchor: operable=true can co-occur with attribution=MISMATCH: 'operable' is computed as lane-state-only (verdict RESOLVED && state ACTIVE), not identity-gated, so an unattributed process querying an active lane sees operable=true with authorized_to_act=false.
a_rows_sample.statement: No rule is violated (authorization still correctly requires MATCH), but the field name invites a human reader to conflate eligibility with authorization -- a legibility/naming finding, not a safety finding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: verdict: RETURN FOR CORRECTION, narrowly scoped -- the delegation contract, the V-3 boundary, and the provider-independence property all stand as built and must not be changed; recommended correction set V-1, V-3, V-5.
a_rows_sample.statement: The overall independent-verification verdict: everything structural passed (including the three PO/ARB-required decisive tests), but three correctness/legibility defects in the asset's core deliverable (making the record truthful and legible) block acceptance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: creating a workflow record to host the correction lane would silently resolve V-8 (whether this work item itself must be a governed workflow record) by implementation, not by PO/ARB authority -- so Governance creates neither the record nor a workaround, and escalates the circularity instead.
a_rows_sample.statement: A worked example of refusing to resolve a governance question 'by omission' (proceeding without a lane) or 'by fiat' (creating the record) when both are live options, and instead surfacing the choice explicitly to the decision authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: repair the three demonstrated defects without reopening the architecture that already passed independent verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: The governing principle of the scoped V-1/V-3/V-5 correction commission, with an explicit 'CRITICAL: do not fix the a8ce5a91->AMBIGUOUS behavior' instruction preserving a correct fail-closed result from being mistaken for a bug.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the correction needs a governed lane -> a lane needs a workflow record -> creating the record would decide V-8 -> V-8 must not be decided by fiat.
a_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential governance circularity disclosed explicitly (with two named possible exits) rather than silently resolved, escalated to PO/ARB for a first-principles determination.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-SESSION-BOOTSTRAP-001 SHALL be registered as a governed work item in the existing workflow model before its correction work proceeds. This does NOT mean AST-017 is adopted; it only means its corrective work is governed.
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB's resolution of the V-8 circularity (Option (a): decide the open governance question first, then create the record by authority, rather than running the correction ungoverned or creating the record silently by implementation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: technical evidence (a process performed a verification) and governed role (that process has an established workflow role) are two separate facts; do not retroactively give a process a workflow role just because its report exists.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly withholds governed-role status from the independent verifier (d1612e03) despite its verification report being accepted as valid technical evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V-1 regression requirement: a lane created-and-cancelled-without-START MUST report recorded_human_start_act=false and stay authorized_to_act=false. Do NOT weaken G-3.
a_rows_sample.statement: A precise, test-shaped acceptance criterion for the V-1 correction, specifying exactly the regression the fix must produce without loosening the START-gate invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V-3 regression requirement: the a8ce5a39 -> AMBIGUOUS case MUST remain AMBIGUOUS -- do NOT 'fix' the live ambiguity by choosing a lane; the correction is only about making the explanation truthful (listing only the matching candidates, not all candidates).
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly separates a correctness improvement (the message) from a behavior that must never change (the ambiguity verdict itself).

a_rows_sample.anchor: the appointed correction actor's concrete identity is a placeholder (claude-code-session:<ACTOR-ID>) that Governance must not fill, adopt, or fabricate -- it must be declared by the appointed actor itself and verified through the existing mechanism.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms 'no process may adopt another process's identity' (INV-ATTR-1/2) even when the governing commission itself needs to name an actor, blocking REGISTER until the actor self-declares.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the candidate declares and reports; it confirms nothing. Eligibility != authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: A worked pattern for a self-appointment-adjacent situation: the candidate process discloses its own prior participation (governance-recording acts on the same work item) rather than silently self-certifying independence, leaving the judgment to PO/ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: identity resolved live from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, not manufactured, not copied from another session, not adopted from a prompt/transcript/scratchpad/historical artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Documents the concrete, environment-derived source of process-identity self-declaration used throughout the batch's governance saga, consistent with INV-ATTR-1/2 (identity is evidential only).

a_rows_sample.anchor: a session bootstrap that resolves a process's lane, role, and authority from the governed record and *fails closed* — on any unresolved fact the answer is "not authorized," never a guess ... a_rows_sample.statement: What exists today: a fail-closed session bootstrap (any unresolved fact answers 'not authorized', never a guess), a read-only presenter of the adopted operating model, and observation-pipeline diagnostics that only check and report, never install or repair. a_rows_sample.anchor: Six-way non-collapse | session-bootstrap.php | [E]

b_rows_sample.anchor: A governed AI session — Claude or DeepSeek — must be able to resolve its own registered lane / role / workflow state / authority deterministically at session start, from the SAME authoritative state, WITHOUT weakening a single governance rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: AST-017's one-line thesis: any governed AI session, regardless of model provider, must be able to deterministically resolve its own lane/role/state/authority from the single authoritative workflow record without weakening any governance rule; 'Resolution is not activation' — the report creates no authority, ownership, or state change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AST-017 holds no fold loop, no transition state machine, no state derivation. Every workflow fact comes from AST-015 invoked as a subprocess
b_rows_sample.statement: AMENDMENT 2 delegation contract: AST-017 delegates every workflow fact (assignment, grant, mutation_owner) to AST-015 via askMechanism(fold/identity/authorized); if the mechanism is unavailable the bootstrap fails closed (UNRESOLVABLE) rather than reading records itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AST-017 performs exactly ONE raw read, in the named function v3HandoffRead() ... the single HANDOFF-to/from-lane fact
b_rows_sample.statement: The one bounded exception to AST-017's read-only delegation is a single named function reading exactly the HANDOFF-to/from-lane fact directly from the raw record, because no AST-015 read command yet exposes it (open finding V-3); regression S16 poisons the raw record to prove the bootstrap still reports fold-derived truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: identity ≠ role ≠ eligibility ≠ authorization ≠ ownership ≠ continuation
b_rows_sample.statement: AST-017's output contract is a six-way separation, each a first-class report block: identity (evidence-only, never a grant input per INV-ATTR-1/2), assignment, activation_prerequisites (the G-3 prerequisites, never a status), grant, mutation_owner, gates, continuation, and meta.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fail-closed mapping: any AMBIGUOUS/UNRESOLVED/UNRESOLVABLE ⇒ operable=false, authorized_to_act=false, current_session_can_continue=false, unresolved_message = missing fact · source · responsible next actor. Never invent; never transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Every non-RESOLVED verdict collapses to a uniform fail-closed report shape naming the missing fact, its source, and the responsible next actor, and never invents identity/authorization or performs a transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $recordedHumanStartAct = $selected['state'] !== 'CREATED'; // AFTER — $recordedHumanStartAct = $selected['state'] === 'ACTIVE';
b_rows_sample.statement: V-1 defect: recorded_human_start_act was derived from 'state !== CREATED', falsely claiming a human START for a lane that reached CANCELLED without ever being STARTED; corrected to derive from 'state === ACTIVE', the fold state AST-015 sets only on START/CONTINUATION.

b_rows_sample.anchor: meta.disambiguation_required rendered describeLanes($candidates) — every discovered candidate, not the ones that actually matched the process selector
b_rows_sample.statement: V-3 defect: the disambiguation message listed every discovered candidate rather than only the ones actually matching the process selector (e.g. listing a non-matching lane V3LANE-C); corrected by tracking an explicit $ambiguousMatches set and rendering only it, verified live to still leave the real a8ce5a39 case AMBIGUOUS without silently selecting a lane.

b_rows_sample.anchor: harness consumers referenced bootstrapping_status; the report emits activation_prerequisites. Mechanism and consumers disagreed.
b_rows_sample.statement: V-5 defect: harness documentation referenced field name bootstrapping_status while the implementation already emitted activation_prerequisites; resolved by canonicalizing activation_prerequisites everywhere (no working code change needed) and pinning a regression asserting bootstrapping_status is never emitted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preservation conditions — all eight survive
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight named preservation properties (single-authority AST-015; AST-017 read-only; V-3 exception bounded to one fact; no second fold/engine; provider independence; ambiguity fail-closed; identity evidence-only; human START boundary intact) were each independently checked and all survive the correction; full suite 50/50 · 566 assertions green.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The regressions S-18/S-19/S-20 were read, then independently reconstructed with fresh hermetic fixtures built through AST-015 in temp dirs ... never touching the live store
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification methodology: rebuild the falsification fixtures from scratch through the canonical mechanism rather than re-running the author's own regression tests, so that a false-positive shared bug in the original tests could not silently pass twice.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the prior verification artifact self-declares verifier d1612e03; the independent-verification registration attributes it to 8a525719 ... the naming inconsistency should be reconciled before the adoption decision
b_rows_sample.statement: A prior verification artifact and its Governance registration attribute the same act to two different process identities (d1612e03 vs 8a525719); both may be genuine (different producing vs registering processes) but the inconsistency should be reconciled before any adoption decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'no record = ungoverned = free' is forbidden reasoning
b_rows_sample.statement: When a work item is named but no authoritative workflow record yet exists for it, the mechanism reports UNRESOLVABLE rather than treating the absence of a record as freedom to act; nothing can be registered or started until the record exists and a lane is attributed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FU-1 · The authoritative workflow store is not durable ... .claude/runtime/workflow/*.json is the authoritative record ... A lost or reset working tree loses every governed lane, every recorded human START act, and therefore every attribution the system relies on.
b_rows_sample.statement: The entire governance chain's trust anchor — the transition log every REGISTER/HANDOFF/START in this batch is written into — lives only in a git-ignored working-tree file with no durability mechanism outside it; a lost or reset working tree would lose every governed lane and every recorded human act, sharpening a previously weaker concern about evidence durability into a concern about the durability of the registration mechanism itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FU-2 · Identity-label extraction cannot distinguish an assignment from a mention ... a8ce5a39 is the registered actor of S5 and, in S6, merely named in prose ... Both lanes therefore 'reference' a8ce5a39, and the resolver reports AMBIGUOUS
b_rows_sample.statement: AST-017's processLabelsReferenced() merges two semantically different matches (a lane's registered actor vs any hex-shaped token mentioned in free prose, e.g. an independence-disclosure sentence naming a prior actor) into one set, producing a false AMBIGUOUS verdict whose surface grows monotonically as governed lanes accumulate prose referencing prior actors by design; the verdict stays safe (fail-closed) but is reasoned about for the wrong cause.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the label character class includes '.', so a label written immediately before a sentence-ending period is captured with the period ... A lane whose only label carried the period would not be attributable to its own actor at all: the actor would resolve UNRESOLVED despite holding an ACTIVE lane.
b_rows_sample.statement: A narrower artifact of the same extraction regex: a label immediately followed by a sentence-ending period is captured with the trailing period attached, which could in the worst case leave a legitimately ACTIVE lane's own actor resolving UNRESOLVED because its only recorded label form does not match.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the corpus contains both a premature "theory closed" declaration and a later falsification that rescinded that closure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Justifies not simply copying the latest 'v1.3 closed' document into a planned consolidated book, citing several already-corrected corpus positions (Truth!=Evaluation!=Determination!=Decision as constitutional; non-explosive contradiction; question/context-relative adequacy; history-preserving non-monotonic state evolution; core operations ASSERT/LINK/REVISE/RETRACT/ISOLATE; parameterized rather than universal measurement arithmetic; ABK-1 downgraded from unique-minimal to candidate-adequate; the Knowledge Gap representable in a power-set structure with empty-set as Zero).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part A — What KnowledgeOS is ... Part S — Theory → architecture → governance
a_rows_sample.statement: A 19-part (A-S) outline for a full theory rewrite is proposed, covering ontological/epistemic primitives, Knowledge State, truth/evidence/evaluation separation, evidence, evaluation, satisfaction/adequacy, Knowledge Gap (Delta_t={r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)}), Zero (contract-relative, not 'everything is true' and not 'numerical distance is zero'), contradiction without explosion, identity/equivalence (=, equiv_sem, approx_{Q,Gamma,O}, provenance/history-sensitive identity), temporal/historical semantics, core operations O_core={ASSERT,LINK,REVISE,RETRACT,ISOLATE}, the transition system K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,o,Gamma_t) with V(K_t)⊆V(K_{t+1}) and H(K_t)⊆H(K_{t+1}), mathematical foundation (projection identifies distinctions: x1~_pi x2 <=> pi(x1)=pi(x2), giving Adequate(pi,Q)=>D_Q⊆Preserved(pi)), statistical foundation, computational foundation (proof!=implementation test!=empirical benchmark), representation reduction/kernel (ABK-1 as validated-adequate not universally-minimal), and theory->architecture->governance ('Architecture does not prove theory. Theory constrains architecture.').

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not call the resulting document simply "Theory v1.3." ... KNOWLEDGEOS — VERIFIED THEORY AND MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION, Consolidated Edition / Theory v2.0
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends naming the rewrite 'Theory v2.0' rather than reusing the contested 'Theory v1.3' name (given contradictory prior closure claims under that name), with a separate historical verification appendix, and classifying every major statement as one of Definition/Axiom/Lemma/Theorem/Corollary/Proposition/Conjecture/Empirical Result/Parameterization/Governance Rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality ≠ Observation ≠ Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Knowledge ≠ Decision ≠ Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A1 (Semantic Separation) opens Part I of the v2.0 rewrite: reality, observation, information, evidence and knowledge are held to occupy different semantic roles unless a formal equivalence is explicitly established, giving the epistemic lifecycle Reality->Observation->Information->Knowledge->Gap->Inquiry->Determination->Decision->Action->New Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If there exist ω1,ω2 ∈ Ω such that ω1≠ω2 and ρ(ω1)=ρ(ω2), then ρ is not injective and therefore cannot uniquely identify the underlying state of reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 3.1 with proof: an observation map rho:Omega->I need not be injective, so KnowledgeOS must never silently infer Observed(x)=>Reality(x).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate(R,Q,Γ) ⟺ 𝓡_req(Q,Γ) ⊆ Dist(R)
b_rows_sample.statement: The Representation Adequacy Principle: a representation is adequate only if it preserves the distinctions required to answer the declared inquiry under context Gamma, avoiding the impossible requirement of preserving every conceivable distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose there exist x1,x2 ∈ X such that x1≠x2 but π(x1)=π(x2). Then any question Q whose required distinction includes x1≠x2 cannot, in general, be answered correctly from π(x) alone.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 16.1 (Loss of Required Distinction), with proof by the impossibility of a deterministic function distinguishing two values a projection maps identically; establishes that a system can be perfectly internally consistent and still epistemically inadequate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_t = {r ∈ Req_t : ¬Sat(K_t,r)} ... Gap = Unsatisfied Requirements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Redefines the Knowledge Gap as a set-theoretic construction (unsatisfied requirements under the current epistemic contract) rather than a subtraction Delta=IdealKnowledge-Knowledge, explicitly rejecting the latter as generally undefined because the two objects need not belong to a common algebraic space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,EC_t) ⟺ Δ_t = ∅ ... Therefore Zero is contract-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Definition 23.1 (Epistemic Zero): Zero means no requirement of the declared epistemic contract remains unsatisfied; explicitly not K_t=Reality and not 'all possible knowledge is known.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Δ_{t+1} ⊆ Δ_t ... every requirement satisfied at t remains satisfied at t+1 ... This theorem depends on the contract remaining fixed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorems 24.1 (Zero Equivalence) and 25.1 (Gap Reduction) are proved, with an explicit limitation that gap comparison across differing contracts (EC_t != EC_{t+1}) requires an explicit compatibility mapping — 'moving the goalposts' is formally blocked by the Contract Compatibility principle GapComparison=>ContractCompatibility.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V(K_t) ⊆ V(K_{t+1}) ∧ H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) ... Historical existence ≠ Current epistemic standing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A6 (Historical Preservation) plus the constitutional distinction between historical existence and current epistemic standing: a proposition can move Supported->Retracted without deleting the historical fact that it was once asserted and supported; replaces 'universal epistemic monotonicity' with this weaker, correct invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth ≠ Evaluation ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A2 (Epistemic Pipeline Separation), with the worked consequence that EVal(p)=Supported does not mean Decision=Permit (a governance policy may instead require HumanReview) — epistemic status is explicitly not equivalent to operational authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p) ⇏ ∀q ∈ 𝒫, q. ... Local contradiction ⇏ Global epistemic collapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Axiom A5 (Non-Explosion): KnowledgeOS explicitly rejects the classical explosion principle as a system rule, requiring contradiction to be scoped and represented rather than collapsing all propositions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 𝒪_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE}
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the frozen candidate core operation interface (introduce an assertion, establish a relation, change content while preserving history, withdraw standing without erasing history, and restrict propagation of a contradiction or dangerous structure), with full preconditions/postconditions/composition laws deferred to later parts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 is a validated candidate-adequate architecture for the target problem class.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly withdraws the earlier claim that ABK-1 is 'the universally unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' as circular, replacing it with the weaker, defensible claim that global minimality remains unproven unless the candidate representation space and equivalence relation are formally characterized.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology defines what kinds of things KnowledgeOS reasons about. Representation defines how those things are encoded.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ontology/representation boundary underlying Part II's many-sorted type system (Ent, Val, Attr, Dim, Prop, Asrt, Obs, Evd, Src, Rel, Evt, St, Ctx, Part, Prov, ES, Req, Inq, EC, Pol, Dec, Act), asserting a database/graph/JSON/RDF/object-model representation is never the ontology itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let D be a value domain and n:D→ℝ a numerical encoding. If no semantic operation corresponding to subtraction is defined on D, then n(x)−n(y) cannot ... be interpreted as a valid semantic difference.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.1 (Representation does not imply arithmetic validity), with proof, establishing that numerical computability of a difference does not by itself establish semantic validity of that difference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(e,p) ⇏ Truth(p).
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposition 2.1, proved by the type-mismatch argument that support is an epistemic evidence-proposition relation while truth is a semantic proposition-model relation with different domains and meanings; called one of the most important anti-confusion principles in KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let R:𝕂→X be a representation function. Suppose there exist K1≠K2 such that R(K1)=R(K2). If there exists an inquiry Q such that Answer(Q,K1,Γ)≠Answer(Q,K2,Γ), then R is inadequate for Q,Γ.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.3 (Semantically lossy representation), with proof, generalizing Part I's Theorem 16.1 to the knowledge-state level and formally establishing why representation adequacy must be question-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status_Γ,EC(p)=σ ... We deliberately do not define one universal ordered list such as Unknown<Supported<Proven<Rejected.
b_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Status is defined as contract- and context-dependent rather than a single universal total order, giving formal meaning to 'unknown' as neither true nor false rather than as a weaker degree of falsity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If Conflict is represented as a local relation on propositions, then the existence of a conflict concerning p does not by itself entail conflict concerning arbitrary q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Theorem 2.5 (Locality theorem for contradiction), with proof, giving the formal ontological grounding for the non-explosion axiom stated in Part I.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT treat stored data as knowledge merely because it is stored.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) close Part II — proposition/evidence separation, observation/proposition separation, decision/action separation, epistemic-status/truth separation, identity/state separation, evidence/truth separation, contract relativity, historical preservation, non-explosion, and representation independence — as the boundaries preventing KnowledgeOS from collapsing into an ordinary information system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth → Evidence → Evaluation → Determination → Decision ... The arrows indicate dependency possibilities, not logical equivalence.

a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a Distinction Conservation Rule for O_core operators: Delta R_req(delta(K,o,Gamma)) subseteq DeclaredChange(o), i.e. an operation may alter state values but cannot collapse any non-declared required distinction -- immediately identified in the same file's second pass as directionally correct but formally ambiguous (Delta R_req suggests a change to the distinction SET rather than to distinction VALUES).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The six core operators are NOT yet established ... the previous operation archaeology explicitly required every operation to be tested for whether it is theory-required, implementation-required, governance-required, representational, derivable, etc. Therefore we cannot yet write O_core=... a_rows_sample.statement: Renames the proposed operator set from O_core to O_cand (Assert, Retract, Supersede, Merge, Split, Isolate), on the grounds that the prior operation-archaeology work requires every operation to be tested for theory-required/implementation-required/governance-required/representational/derivable status before it can be called core; specifies the necessary test dimensions: indispensability, derivability, compositionality, history-sensitivity, distinction-preservation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Isolate especially needs proof ... Isolate may instead manipulate evaluation propagation or boundary. So we must determine whether Isolate: K -> K' is actually a state operation, or whether it is: Isolate: EVal -> EVal' or even: Isolate: Gamma -> Gamma'. This is a DDD boundary question as well as a mathematical one. Until that is resolved: Isolate in O_core ? remains OPEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: Singles out Isolate as needing separate proof from the other five candidate operators (which manipulate knowledge content/state): Isolate might instead operate on evaluation propagation (EVal->EVal') or on context (Gamma->Gamma') rather than on state (K->K'), framed as both a mathematical typing question and a DDD boundary-ownership question; whether Isolate belongs in O_core at all is left explicitly OPEN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Distinction Conservation Rule needs one correction ... R_req is a set of distinctions, whereas Delta R_req sounds like a change in the required-distinction set itself. Those are not necessarily the same thing. We should instead define something like: Changed_d(K,K') for the actual change in distinction d. Then: {d in R_req | Changed_d(K,K')} subseteq DeclaredChange(o). ... An operation may change a required distinction only when that change is explicitly declared by the operation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Distinction Conservation Rule's notation: replaces the ambiguous Delta R_req(delta(K,o,Gamma)) subseteq DeclaredChange(o) with a precise Changed_d(K,K') predicate for the actual change in one distinction d, giving {d in R_req | Changed_d(K,K')} subseteq DeclaredChange(o) -- stated as a potentially strong constitutional law: an operation may change a required distinction only when that change is explicitly declared by the operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic equivalence is close, but the proposed definition is too strong ... It makes semantic equivalence dependent on the currently declared question universe Q ... equality of all required distinction values is not automatically equivalent to behavioral equivalence. Two states might agree on the currently tested distinctions but differ under a future permitted operation. We therefore need: equiv_sem and equiv_O and potentially: equiv_{sem,Q,Gamma,O}. This connects directly to the earlier result that semantic equivalence cannot be fully settled until the operation universe is known.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the proposed R_req-grounded semantic-equivalence definition: agreement on all currently-declared-question-required distinctions is not automatically behavioral equivalence, since two states could agree on tested distinctions yet differ under a future permitted operation; introduces equiv_O (operation-relative equivalence) alongside equiv_sem, generalizing to equiv_{sem,Q,Gamma,O} -- explicitly connecting to a prior corpus result that semantic equivalence cannot be fully settled until the operation universe (O_cand/O_core) is known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_core is still not closed ... From DDD architecture, these are clearly different categories. I would separate: State mutation (Assert, Retract, Supersede, Merge, Split); Evidence relation (LinkEvidence, Support, Refute); Query/read (Query, Compare, Trace); Assurance/governance (Validate, Authorize); Presentation/explanation (Explain). a_rows_sample.anchor: there is an important DDD point: delta should probably operate on domain events/commands only after we have separated command, event, observation and state transition. We should not blindly call every operation an event.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is the point where we should stop adding philosophical interpretation and start doing systematic operator discovery. ... Given a time-varying knowledge state K_t, what operations can the KnowledgeOS Kernel perform, under what conditions, and what mathematical invariants must every operation preserve? ... Strategic Discovery -> Tactical Discovery -> Formal Operator Catalogue -> Simulation -> Canonicalization. ... we discover operators first; we do not declare them canonical merely because the Gītā suggests them.
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares the pivot point of the whole Gita-kernel track: stop adding philosophical interpretation, start systematic operator discovery, framed as the real engineering question (what operations can the Kernel perform, under what conditions, preserving what invariants). Proposes a five-phase discovery pipeline: Strategic Discovery -> Tactical Discovery -> Formal Operator Catalogue -> Simulation -> Canonicalization, with the discipline that operators are discovered first and never declared canonical merely because the Gita suggests them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel: (K_t,O_t,C_t) -> (K_{t+1},E_t) ... Buddhi sits inside this transformation ... Input -> Buddhi -> Kernel Operation -> K_{t+1}. The Kernel does not blindly transform knowledge. It must determine: Is this admissible? Is it new? Is it contradictory? Does it strengthen an existing proposition? Does it invalidate something? Does it require qualification? Does it change a dimension? Does it require action? Does it merely represent uncertainty?
b_rows_sample.statement: Models the Kernel as a bounded domain: Kernel: (K_t,O_t,C_t) -> (K_{t+1},E_t) [current state, observations/input, contextual constraints -> resulting state, evidence/audit], with Buddhi sitting inside the transformation (Input -> Buddhi -> Kernel Operation -> K_{t+1}), enumerating nine discrimination questions the Kernel must ask (admissible? new? contradictory? strengthens? invalidates? needs qualification? changes a dimension? requires action? represents uncertainty?).

b_rows_sample.anchor: SD-1 Acquisition operators: Acquire, Observe, Receive, Detect, Discover ... Observation != Proposition != Knowledge ... SD-2 Discrimination operators (the Buddhi family): Distinguish, Compare, Classify, Separate, Accept, Reject, Defer, Contradict ... P1 != P2 does not automatically mean P1 is false. Buddhi must distinguish: different, contradictory, more specific, superseding, compatible, incomparable, unknown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the first two of nine candidate operator families for systematic (not philosophy-first) discovery: SD-1 Acquisition operators (Acquire, Observe, Receive, Detect, Discover), reinforcing Observation != Proposition != Knowledge with a worked HTTP-500 example; SD-2 Discrimination operators, the 'Buddhi family' (Distinguish, Compare, Classify, Separate, Accept, Reject, Defer, Contradict), noting P1!=P2 does not imply P1 is false -- Buddhi must distinguish seven distinct relations: different, contradictory, more specific, superseding, compatible, incomparable, unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SD-3 Knowledge construction operators: Create, Compose, Derive, Infer, Corroborate, Associate, Relate ... P1+P2+R -> P3 could represent a derived proposition. Derivation != Corroboration. ... SD-4 Knowledge revision operators: Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire ... K_t != K_{t+1} is normal rather than exceptional ... K_{t+1} preserves sufficient history to explain K_t -> K_{t+1}. That immediately connects the operator problem to the existing H/replay work.
b_rows_sample.statement: SD-3 Knowledge construction operators (Create, Compose, Derive, Infer, Corroborate, Associate, Relate), with P1+P2+R->P3 as a derived-proposition example and the standing distinction Derivation != Corroboration. SD-4 Knowledge revision operators (Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire), grounded in K_t != K_{t+1} being normal, with a proposed central invariant that K_{t+1} must preserve sufficient history to explain the K_t->K_{t+1} transition, explicitly connecting the operator-discovery problem to the corpus's existing H/replay structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SD-6 Relationship operators: Member, Relate, Compare, Contradict, Support, Depend, Supersede, Derive, Trace ... whether R is merely a data structure or whether it is itself the result of Kernel operations. ... SD-9 Action operators ... Action/Event/Policy as external to the epistemic projection ... Knowledge transformation vs World transformation ... K_t -Buddhi-> Decision -Action-> W_{t+1} -Omega-> O_{t+1} -Qualify-> K_{t+1}. This creates a closed epistemic feedback loop.
b_rows_sample.statement: SD-6 Relationship operators (Member, Relate, Compare, Contradict, Support, Depend, Supersede, Derive, Trace), raising whether the relation component R is a data structure or itself the result of Kernel operations. SD-9 Action operators, distinguishing Knowledge transformation from World transformation (since the verification lane treats Action/Event/Policy as external to the epistemic projection), giving a closed epistemic feedback loop K_t --Buddhi--> Decision --Action--> W_{t+1} --Omega--> O_{t+1} --Qualify--> K_{t+1}, offered as a strong interpretation of the Gita's Karma/action distinction without claiming the Gita invented the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every valid Kernel operation must preserve KnowledgeOS state integrity. ... I(K_t) => I(K_{t+1}) for every permitted transformation. Provenance preservation: Pi(K_{t+1}) supseteq Pi_required(K_t). Temporal consistency: a later state must not silently erase the fact that an earlier state existed. Identity consistency: an operation must not accidentally create two identities for one object. Relation consistency ... Evidence consistency: a proposition cannot become stronger without an appropriate epistemic basis. This last one is especially important for AI-generated knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'every valid Kernel operation must preserve KnowledgeOS state integrity' as a central research question, requiring discovery of an invariant set I={I_1,...,I_n} with I(K_t) => I(K_{t+1}) for every permitted transformation, exemplified by five candidate invariants: provenance preservation (Pi(K_{t+1}) supseteq Pi_required(K_t)), temporal consistency (a later state must not silently erase that an earlier state existed), identity consistency (no accidental double-identity for one object), relation consistency (a recorded relation must be preserved or explicitly revised), and evidence consistency (a proposition cannot become stronger without appropriate epistemic basis) -- the last flagged as especially important for AI-generated knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 291 -- KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL OPERATOR DISCOVERY. Strategic Discovery: discover all epistemic transformation families, all state transitions, all primitive transitions, all Buddhi/discrimination functions, all Zero/gap functions, all knowledge-revision functions, all relation transformations, all temporal transformations, all purification candidates, all action/feedback transformations. Tactical Discovery: Input -> Preconditions -> Transformation -> Output -> Evidence -> Provenance -> Invariants. Mathematical Discovery: closure, deterministic, idempotent, compositional, reversible, monotonic. DDD Discovery: Aggregate boundary, Entity, Value Object, Domain Service, Domain Event, invariant, command, decision, policy, lifecycle -- without assuming that every mathematical operator becomes a software method. Gītā Discovery: for every surviving operator ask does the Gītā independently illuminate this operation? Gītā correspondence != KnowledgeOS derivation. Zero Discovery: what can this operation prove that it does not know?
b_rows_sample.statement: Names and structures the proposed research programme 'STEP 291 -- KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL OPERATOR DISCOVERY' with six phases: Strategic Discovery (10 categories of transformation families to discover); Tactical Discovery (Input->Preconditions->Transformation->Output->Evidence->Provenance->Invariants per candidate); Mathematical Discovery (closure, determinism, idempotence, compositionality, reversibility, monotonicity); DDD Discovery (Aggregate boundary, Entity, Value Object, Domain Service, Domain Event, invariant, command, decision, policy, lifecycle -- without assuming every operator becomes a software method); Gita Discovery (for every surviving operator, ask whether the Gita independently illuminates it, preserving Gita correspondence != KnowledgeOS derivation); and Zero Discovery (for every operation, ask what it can prove it does not know -- called possibly the deepest part of the entire Kernel).

b_rows_sample.anchor: the document's proposed Step 291 is directionally right: KnowledgeOS Kernel Operator Discovery. But I would change its mission. Not: Discover the complete operator space. Instead: Construct and audit the candidate operational vocabulary required by the currently ratified KnowledgeOS state model, while proving neither completeness nor canonicality unless independently established. That is much stronger scientifically.
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises S2273's proposed Step 291 mission: not 'discover the complete operator space' (completeness cannot easily be demonstrated) but 'construct and audit the candidate operational vocabulary required by the currently ratified KnowledgeOS state model, while proving neither completeness nor canonicality unless independently established' -- judged much stronger scientifically.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They may support the same proposition p=HasVersion(S,v1) while remaining distinct evidence objects. Therefore we need at least three relations: Identity, Equality, Support. These must not be conflated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes via a two-observation example (o1 by System A at t1, o2 by System B at t2, both supporting the same proposition p) that Identity, Equality, and Support must be three distinct, non-conflatable relations: distinct observations can support the same proposition without being identical or equal to each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS may require domain identity in addition to mathematical equality ... a possible distinction is: StructuralEqual(x,y) versus SameIdentity(x,y). This is not yet an accepted KnowledgeOS definition. It is a required question.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses object-level StructuralEqual(x,y) versus SameIdentity(x,y) as a required, not-yet-answered distinction: two records may be structurally identical while referring to different historical occurrences, so domain identity may be needed beyond ordinary mathematical equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There are at least four possibilities. A. Syntactic equality ... B. Semantic equality ... C. Observational equality ... D. Provenance-sensitive equality ... These are not interchangeable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines four non-interchangeable candidate Knowledge-State equality relations: syntactic (byte/structural identity), semantic (same knowledge semantics), observational (same result under every permitted observation), and provenance-sensitive (content and relevant provenance equivalent).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1={p,e1} and K2={p,e2} where e1!=e2 but Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p). Should K1=K2? There is no obvious answer. ... This proves that equality cannot be defined until we know what constitutes semantically essential information. Equality depends on the ontology and semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a worked counterexample (two states differing only in which distinct evidence item supports the same proposition) showing equality is undecidable until it is settled whether provenance is semantically constitutive of knowledge identity or merely metadata -- concluding equality is ontology/semantics-dependent, not free-standing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mandate explicitly tells us not to assume this dependency ordering [G1->G2->G3]. ... the dependency graph is more accurately: Ontology -> State Representation -> Semantic Identity -> Equality ... So G1->G3 is plausible, but G1->G2->G3 is not established.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a previously assumed linear dependency ordering (G1: what is a KnowledgeState -> G2: what is epistemic status -> G3: what is equality) into a revised chain Ontology -> State Representation -> Semantic Identity -> Equality, with epistemic status interacting with both representation and equality rather than sitting strictly between state-definition and equality; the direct G1->G2->G3 chain is explicitly downgraded to not established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The propositions may refer to different times ... Then there is no contradiction. This demonstrates that contradiction cannot be determined from proposition content alone. ... A better candidate is: Contradicts(p1,p2,c) ... contradiction is likely a derived semantic relation, not a primitive field o
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-interval example (HasVersion(S,v1) valid on [t1,t2), HasVersion(S,v2) valid on [t2,t3)) that two propositions with conflicting content are not automatically contradictory, since contradiction depends on context c as well as content; concludes contradiction is a derived semantic relation Contradicts(p1,p2,c), not a primitive Knowledge-State field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: with both assert validity over exactly the same interval ... If the domain invariant is: forall t: #Version(S,t)<=1, then Contradicts(p1,p2)=true. ... Contradiction required: proposition semantics; temporal validity; domain constraints. Contradiction is not merely a property of two strings.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a strong-contradiction example: two version propositions over the identical time interval, evaluated against an explicit domain invariant (a service has at most one version at any time) actually do produce Contradicts=true, demonstrating contradiction requires jointly proposition semantics, temporal validity, and domain constraints -- it is a relation evaluated under a semantic regime, not a syntactic property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A logical regime could define Contradiction_L. A temporal regime could define Contradiction_T. A probabilistic regime might instead calculate P(p1|E) and P(p2|E). These need not produce the same classification. Contradiction may be regime-relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that contradiction may be regime-relative: a logical regime, a temporal regime, and a probabilistic regime applied to the same pair of propositions need not agree on whether a contradiction exists -- a stronger claim than merely 'KnowledgeOS supports contradictions', and supportive of a multi-regime architecture operating over a common substrate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(p)=0.7 ... It could represent: probability of truth; confidence in an observation; reliability of a source; posterior probability; frequency in a population; degree of belief; probability of an answer. These are mathematically different quantities. 0.7 alone has no epistemic semantics.

b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 3 distinct sameness relations for KnowledgeOS -- object equality (are two knowledge objects the same per the object model), Knowledge-State equivalence (are two states indistinguishable for all semantically relevant operations), and history equivalence (are two histories equivalent with respect to resulting semantic behavior) -- explicitly forbidding their collapse into one relation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x1=(id=42,content=A) and x2=(id=42,content=B). They may represent different versions of the same knowledge entity. Identity persistence != value equality. This is exactly what Revision requires.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves identity persistence and value equality are distinct via a minimal worked example (same id, different content = two versions of the same entity), noting this is exactly the distinction Revision requires to exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x=(i,v,s,p,m) [identity, value, status, provenance, metadata] -- not yet the final Knowledge Object definition. It is a diagnostic model. ... =_I identity equality, =_V content equality, =_S full structural equality, =_E semantic equality [the least trivial to define].
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a diagnostic (not final) 5-field Knowledge Object model x=(identity,value,status,provenance,metadata) and defines 4 candidate object-equality relations over it (identity-only, content-only, full-structural, and semantic equality -- the last flagged as most important and least trivial to define).

b_rows_sample.anchor: =_I cannot by itself be the semantic equality relation [fails Revise, which requires semantic change while identity persists]. ... Content equality cannot replace identity [fails Merge/Supersede, which must distinguish independently-created identical-content objects].
b_rows_sample.statement: Proves both identity-only equality and content-only equality are individually insufficient as the semantic equality relation: identity-only equality cannot represent Revise (which needs semantic change while identity persists); content-only equality cannot represent Merge/Supersede (which must distinguish two independently-created objects with identical content).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 equiv_K K2 iff no mandatory KnowledgeOS observation or transformation can distinguish them. Formally: forall O in mathcal-O: O(K1)=O(K2). b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge-State equivalence observationally (agreement on every semantically relevant observation), then states the stronger transformation-congruence requirement that equivalence must be preserved by every valid transformation -- the critical test for whether the proposed equivalence is too coarse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ~_H H2 iff all permitted future operation sequences produce equivalent states. b_rows_sample.anchor: F(H1)=F(H2) iff H1 ~_H H2 would mean that the state representation exactly captures the behavioral equivalence classes. That would be a major theoretical result. We have not demonstrated this yet.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ideal biconditional quotient criterion (F(H1)=F(H2) iff H1 and H2 are behaviorally equivalent) as the major unproven theoretical result the whole state-abstraction programme is aiming at.

b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the counterexample-class methodology (from S1621) to 4 specific classes -- provenance, revision history, identity-vs-content, identity-vs-status -- each showing content-only or identity-only state abstractions fail whenever some mandatory operation actually observes the discarded distinction, with each case's status remaining conditional on which operations are mandatory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity -> Object equality -> State equality/equivalence -> Behavioral/history equivalence. But this should not be interpreted as a strict mathematical hierarchy where each relation is automatically derived from the previous one. They are separate semantic constructs connected by explicit rules.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a suggestive but explicitly non-derivational ordering of 4 sameness concepts (identity, object equality, state equivalence, behavioral/history equivalence), warning against treating it as a strict hierarchy where each is automatically derivable from the last -- they remain separate constructs connected only by explicit rules.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OperationalIdentity(x) if exists T in T such that changing id(x) can change T(K,c). ... Relevant(p) if there exists a mandatory operation T and states K1,K2 differing only in p such that T(K1,c) not-equiv_K T(K2,c). Then p cannot be discarded from the semantic state representation unless it is suppl
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes identity-relevance into a fully general 'operational relevance' test for any candidate property p: p is Relevant if some mandatory operation and a pair of states differing only in p produce non-equivalent outcomes, in which case p cannot be discarded from the semantic state unless supplied externally -- giving a single principled, uniform criterion applicable to identity, provenance, policy, evidence, or any other candidate field.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K* = minimum information sufficient to preserve all mandatory behavioral distinctions. Not: K*=everything ever observed. And not: K*=smallest tuple someone can invent. This is the mathematically meaningful notion of minimality.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the minimal-state principle in its final form: K* is the minimum information sufficient to preserve all mandatory behavioral distinctions -- explicitly neither an unbounded record of everything ever observed nor an arbitrarily small invented tuple.

b_rows_sample.statement: States the formal admissibility criterion (Proposition 258-A) as the definitive version of the congruence/commuting-diagram requirement first developed in Step 248 (S1608): a state abstraction F is semantically admissible only if every mandatory transformation factors through it via a corresponding state-level function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Does provenance belong in K? can now be answered experimentally. We do not ask philosophically. We ask: exists T: F(H1)=F(H2) but F(T_H(H1)) != F(T_H(H2))? If yes, F is insufficient. Then either: enrich K; supply the missing information as explicit context; remove the operation from the semantic cor
b_rows_sample.statement: Converts the recurring philosophical provenance-placement question into a purely operational test, and gives an explicit 3-way resolution menu when the test fails (enrich K, supply the information as explicit external context, or remove the offending operation from the semantic core) -- noting only the first two options preserve the operation itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K should be defined extensionally through behavioral sufficiency, not compositionally through an arbitrary tuple. ... Do not start with K=(a,b,c,d). Start with: Which distinctions must survive for all valid operations? Then derive the minimal state.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the step's deepest and most general finding: Knowledge State should be defined EXTENSIONALLY through behavioral sufficiency (what distinctions must survive for all valid operations) rather than COMPOSITIONALLY by inventing a tuple of fields and justifying it afterward -- a reversal of the corpus's dominant historical methodology for proposing kernels.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The earlier candidate K=(K,C,T,E,A) should therefore be treated as a meta-structure, not automatically as the mathematical state itself. ... b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity != Equality. Object equality != State equivalence. State equivalence != History equivalence. A valid state abstraction must satisfy transformation congruence. Operation dependence does not imply state membership. Minimality must be defined behaviorally.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates 6 established results from Step 258: Identity!=Equality; Object equality!=State equivalence; State equivalence!=History equivalence; valid state abstractions must satisfy transformation congruence; operation dependence never implies state membership; minimality must be defined behaviorally, not by inspection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operations -> Observations -> Equivalence -> State quotient -> Minimal K, rather than: Invent K -> try to justify it afterward. ... b_rows_sample.anchor: The governing criterion is: F_i(H_1)=F_i(H_2) must imply F_i(\widehat T(H_1,c)) = F_i(\widehat T(H_2,c))
b_rows_sample.statement: A candidate Knowledge-State abstraction F_i:H->K_i is sufficient for a mandatory transformation T over admissible context c iff F_i(H1)=F_i(H2) implies F_i(That(H1,c))=F_i(That(H2,c)); strengthened to require an actual state-level transformation T_i:K_i x C -> K_i such that F_i(That(H,c)) = T_i(F_i(H),c) for all admissible H,c (a commuting square between history-level and state-level transformations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: In particular: Definition of K != Adequacy of K, and: Congruence criterion valid != KnowledgeOS satisfies congruence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-correction of the immediately preceding step: a mathematical definition of K, a candidate representation of K, an abstraction F:H->K, and the claim that F is sufficient for the transformation family are four distinct claims that must not be conflated; Step 258 wrongly treated K as already a well-defined state abstraction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Not every operation has the form: T:K -> K. ... Assess:K x X -> Assessment ... Authorize:Actor x Action x Policy -> Decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Operations must first be classified into (1) knowledge-state transformations, (2) epistemic assessments, (3) governance operations, (4) audit/history operations, (5) observation operations; not every legitimate KnowledgeOS operation is an endomorphism T:K->K — e.g. Assess:K x X -> Assessment and Authorize:Actor x Action x Policy -> Decision are non-state-closing operations, and only state-transforming operations enter the primary congruence test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Now introduce a revision rule dependent on lineage: Revise(x_1,x_2) is permitted only if: Origin(x_1) in ApprovedSources.
b_rows_sample.statement: Conditional counterexample sketch for candidate F_A (artifact-set state) under Revise: if revision eligibility depends on Origin(x1) (an approved-sources lineage rule) while F_A discards origin, two histories with equal F_A images can differ in whether a subsequent Revise is valid, which would falsify F_A's congruence — but this is CONDITIONAL, not PROVEN, unless the corpus actually establishes that revision eligibility depends on origin.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge is the strongest initial discriminator ... If the resulting provenance must distinguish Source_1 from Source_2, then F_A(\widehat{Merge}(H_A)) != F_A(\widehat{Merge}(H_B)).
b_rows_sample.statement: Conditional counterexample sketch for candidate F_A under Merge, described as the strongest initial discriminator among the tested operations: if two histories reach the same artifact x1 from different sources (Source_1 vs Source_2) with F_A(H_A)=F_A(H_B)={x1}, and a subsequent Merge(x1,x2) must record provenance distinguishing Source_1 from Source_2, then F_A fails congruence — again only if provenance is established as semantically observable by Merge, which the governing prompt requires testing (alongside evidence, replay, validation, implementation needs) before deciding whether Evidence/provenance belongs inside or outside K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: All transformations are K -> K | REFUTED as a universal assumption
b_rows_sample.statement: The results table explicitly marks the assumption that all KnowledgeOS transformations have signature K->K as REFUTED as a universal assumption (distinguished from the still-CANDIDATE status of F:H->K as a useful abstraction model, and from several UNRESOLVED items: whether history can be discarded, whether provenance must be inside or can remain outside K, whether the transformation family is closed, whether current K is globally sufficient, whether a minimal K exists).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We cannot perform a valid global congruence proof until the mandatory transformation family is itself sufficiently closed. ... the quantifier forall T in T has no determinate meaning if T is incomplete.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central negative result of the step: a valid global congruence proof is impossible while the mandatory transformation family T is not itself closed, because the universal quantifier 'for all T in T' is not well-defined over an incomplete set; this reinforces the required sequencing Transformation Inventory -> Semantic Classification -> Congruence, rather than jumping to K -> Congruence in isolation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A finite test set can establish: Congruent_{tested}(F). It does not automatically establish: Congruent_{global}(F).
b_rows_sample.statement: Local/tested congruence (survival of a finite, executed test set) must be distinguished from global congruence (a formal proof over the fully specified domain and transformation family); an executed test yields only 'evidence of survival', never 'proof of universal congruence'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This also explains why Step 260 must come after Step 259. Minimality asks whether K* is the coarsest sufficient abstraction. But we cannot establish sufficiency until we know which operations must be preserved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sequencing principle: no valid minimality proof (Step 260, testing whether K* = H/equiv is the coarsest sufficient state abstraction) can precede the operation registry and congruence-matrix analysis (Step 259), since minimality presupposes knowledge of which operations a sufficient state must preserve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A bounded context state is legitimate only if its externally observable behavior does not depend on information that the context has discarded. ... K1 equiv_K K2 must imply identical behavior under the context's published operations.
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation of the congruence criterion: a bounded-context state representation is legitimate only when its externally observable behavior under the context's published operations does not depend on information the context's state has discarded — i.e. the congruence test is a rigorous check for an accidentally omitted domain invariant, not mathematical decoration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We must not assume: Statistical Sufficiency => KnowledgeOS Operational Sufficiency. That requires proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistical interpretation: two histories can produce the same estimated distribution P_theta under a distributional candidate state F_E, yet still be distinguishable by a future transformation dependent on information not identifiable from that distribution; statistical sufficiency must not be assumed to imply KnowledgeOS operational sufficiency without separate proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 259 establishes the formal mechanism by which candidate Knowledge-State abstractions can be falsified, but it does not yet establish that any candidate abstraction is globally sufficient. ... if the quotient does not exist in the required usable form, that is a valid research result.
b_rows_sample.statement: Conservative step verdict: the congruence-falsification mechanism is established but no candidate is proven globally sufficient; Step 260 is set up to test — not assume — existence, uniqueness, representability, computability, decidability, composability, equality, membership and identity of the candidate minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (H1 equiv H2 iff no mandatory operation can distinguish them), explicitly allowing a negative result (the quotient not existing in usable form) as a valid outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ≈ H2 iff every permitted observation produces the same result: ∀O∈𝒪: O(H1)=O(H2). ... This is the relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observational equivalence for histories (H1 approx H2 iff every permitted observation O produces the same result) and for states (K1 approx K2 iff every permitted state observation agrees) is identified as the same relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient; notably it does not require internal representations to be identical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ≡_K K2 ⟺ ∀O∈𝒪_K: O(K1)=O(K2) ... 𝒪_K is not yet completely closed. Therefore this is a candidate formal definition, not a completed theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate formal definition of Knowledge-State equality as purely observational/behavioral: K1 equiv_K K2 iff every permitted state observation O in the (not-yet-closed) set O_K agrees on K1 and K2; explicitly a candidate, not a completed theorem, because O_K is not yet closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Equality → Congruence → Quotient → Minimality. This is the correct dependency direction.
b_rows_sample.statement: If K1 equiv_K K2 (no permitted observation distinguishes them) and all mandatory operations preserve that equivalence, equiv_K becomes the congruence relation needed for the minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (Step 260) — establishing the dependency direction Equality -> Congruence -> Quotient -> Minimality as correct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation-sufficiency test F(H1) = F(H2) ⇒ F(T(H1,i)) = F(T(H2,i)) — executed, congruent for every input tested. See artifact F.
b_rows_sample.statement: The transformation-sufficiency (congruence) test F(H1)=F(H2) => F(T(H1,i))=F(T(H2,i)) was executed and found congruent for every tested input, with full detail deferred to a separate artifact F — direct empirical support for the K=(A,R) abstraction passing the Step-259 congruence criterion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The model is executable, so removal is testable. The phrase MINIMAL KERNEL is therefore earned — but only in the sense step 254 names: Minimality(K | 𝒯), relative to the transformation set. Not ontological necessity. A richer 𝒯 could force more.
b_rows_sample.statement: Minimality caveat: the removal-based necessity audit only earns Minimality(K|T) relative to the specific tested transformation set T (per step 254's framing), never ontological necessity of the components — a richer transformation set could force additional components to become necessary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F(Hx) = F(Hy) ? False — different states, so congruence is NOT tested by this pair ... A congruence test requires two DIFFERENT histories producing the SAME state. Two of my first three attempts were vacuous, and would have "passed" while proving nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-disclosed methodological failure: two of the first three attempted congruence-test constructions used history pairs that already produced different F-images, meaning congruence was never actually being tested (a vacuous pass); a valid congruence test requires two DIFFERENT histories that fold to the SAME state F(H1)=F(H2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hr = [assert A1, assert A4] ; Hs = [assert A4, assert A1] ... F(Hr) = F(Hs) = True ... i = relate(A1,A4,supersedes) -> congruent: True ... i = assert A2 -> congruent: True ... i = relate(A4,A1,refines) -> congruent: True ... F(H1) = F(H3) where H3 re-asserts A1 (idempotence) -> congruent: True. No c
b_rows_sample.statement: Valid executed congruence test: order-reversed histories Hr=[assert A1, assert A4] and Hs=[assert A4, assert A1] satisfy the precondition F(Hr)=F(Hs); three different subsequent operations (relate-supersedes, assert, relate-refines) are each tested and found congruent, plus an idempotence test (re-asserting A1); no counterexample is found across these tests.

b_rows_sample.statement: Structural (by-construction) explanation for why congruence held in every test: T's derived signature K x Op x Policy x Authority -harpoon-> K x Outcome does not include History in its domain, so T cannot depend on it — a function cannot depend on an argument it does not receive.
